Saudi Arabia's closure of a major oil pipeline after a recent attack is raising fears that global energy markets in crisis because of the war with Iran could face even starker shortages, pushing prices higher for fuel and other essentials.

The largest oil producer in the Middle East closed its East-West pipeline on Friday after the attack, which it blamed on drones from Iranian-backed militias in Iraq. Two regional officials told The Associated Press that repairs could take three to five weeks.

The pipeline is crucial to getting some crude out of the Middle East by shipping it to the Red Sea rather than through the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which roughly a fifth of the world’s oil supply passed before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in February.

Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels have seized islands along key Red Sea shipping routes, further threatening Saudi exports. And while several limited alternatives remain, including trickles of tanker traffic in Hormuz, experts warn more supply shocks and higher prices straining households could pile up. Brent crude, the international standard, traded at more than $105 a barrel Monday.

Here's what we know:

What is the East-West pipeline?

Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline stretches some 1,200 kilometers (746 miles) across the desert nation — carrying oil from a processing facility near the Persian Gulf westward to the Red Sea. There, crude is typically loaded onto tankers that head north towards Europe via the Suez Canal or south through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, on the way to Asia.

The pipeline was built in the 1980s amid fears that Tehran would disrupt shipping through Hormuz during the Iran-Iraq war. And for the first six months of the current war, it was crucial to keeping at least some oil flowing out of the Middle East while most tanker traffic in Hormuz remained at a standstill.

Rystad Energy said Monday that an average 2.6 million to 4 million barrels of oil a day moved through the pipeline and out of the Red Sea port of Yanbu since late August — a volume it said is now at risk of “disappearing from the market.”

Four million barrels per day is about 4% of the global oil supply, according to the International Energy Agency. Saudi Arabia produced nearly 10 million barrels of oil a day in September 2025, but was down to 6 million barrels per day in August, the IEA said.

Janiv Shah, vice president of oil markets for Rystad Energy, noted the recent jump in Brent prices proves the market is already responding to “a significant loss of supply.” Saudi inventories could sustain exports in the coming days, but that could “change quickly," Shah added.

Where oil flows from the Middle East stand now

The Strait of Hormuz is still top of mind. Before the war, about 20 million barrels passed through Hormuz each day.

Some tankers are again traversing the strait, but traffic is well below what it once was. Maritime data company Lloyd’s List Intelligence counted 90 transits in the first week of September. Before the war, about 130 ships passed through daily.

The Houthis have also tightened their hold on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a vital passage for the southern Red Sea. Analysts at Melius Research estimated that about 3 million barrels of oil a day were moving through Bab el-Mandeb in early September, but noted Monday that “it’s likely zero now.”

Because of Houthi attacks, most Saudi traffic from Yanbu went north to the Mediterranean, either via the Suez Canal or Egypt’s SUMED pipeline. But the Houthis have also begun targeting Saudi shipping in the north.

Salvatore Mercogliano, a professor of maritime history at Campbell University in North Carolina, noted that at least Hormuz is still on the table.

“If this (East-West pipeline) was the only method for Saudi Arabia to get their oil out it would be absolutely cataclysmic,” he said. “But since the Hormuz route has opened back up — not completely but opened up some — it’s not the death knell for Saudi Arabia. They’re getting oil out.”

Prices keep climbing

Supply squeezes have led to soaring prices worldwide. And analysts warn that the latest disruptions could bring even more pain for consumers in the coming weeks and months.

One of the most immediate consequences is the cost of fuel and household energy bills. Countries in Asia and Africa, which rely more heavily on imports from the Middle East, have experienced some of the starkest shocks.

In Nigeria, for example, diesel prices are now 92% higher than they were in late February, and gasoline prices are up nearly 61%, according to energy tracker Global Petrol Prices. Countries including Indonesia (diesel up 87% and gas up 38%) and Lebanon (diesel up 80% and gas up 46%) have also seen steep spikes.

In the U.S., the price per gallon of regular gasoline was nearly $4.32 on average Monday, up almost 45% from the $2.98 seen before the war, according to motor club AAA. Diesel hit another all-time high (without accounting for inflation) of $6.23 per gallon on average Monday, up nearly 66% from the start of the war.

The cost of diesel, in particular, makes its way into other goods because the fuel is used for long-haul trucks and other delivery networks, as well as farm equipment.

“An inflationary spillover is likely,” warned Melius Research analysts on Monday, pointing to the war's squeeze on essentials like fertilizer as well as energy sources. “The diesel crunch is also coming ahead of the U.S. harvesting and heating season.”

____

Anderson reported from New York. Associated Press writer Samy Magdy in Cairo contributed.

Hundreds of people gathered on Monday at a mass funeral in eastern Congo to mourn 27 young victims of a fire that engulfed two schools, as families wept and officials laid down wreaths and made speeches.

A fire swept through two adjacent schools last week in the city of Bukavu in eastern Congo, triggering a stampede as students tried to flee the building. At least 27 students were killed and dozens were injured, according to local authorities.

The fire Thursday started at a house before spreading to the two adjoining schools, local neighborhood administrator Moïse Lubala told The Associated Press. He said several students were trapped inside Furaha secondary school and some suffocated. The cause of the fire remains unknown, but the area is densely populated with wooden houses.

Medical staff were struggling to keep track of the exact number of injured because there were so many, he said.

Annunciat Kujirabwinja Zagabe came to the funeral Monday to say goodbye to her 13-year-old grandson, Tuonane Machara wa Kidogo.

“The last time I spoke to him, I urged him to study hard so that one day he could become like his teachers, and he was doing well at school,” she said barely holding back tears, as her voice broke down.

“That is why I am in such deep distress. I remember his journey through school up to the eighth grade without ever failing a single year, and now, he has died just like that, without even falling ill. He left home for school and simply died. It is horrific.”

Alice Ambika Musafiri, one of the teachers, wept uncontrollably as she recalled the fire.

Musafiri said she was haunted by children's voices calling for help.

“Ma’am, I’m being trampled!" she remembered them crying.

“My child, I can’t reach you,” she yelled back. “Wait until I get the one I have now out first.”

But as much as she tried, some students were still suffocated by the crowd.

“My children, I had no way to save you. I lacked the strength; that is why I saved who I could,” she told the AP, while a friend held her so she wouldn’t fall down from the emotions. “Oh God, those voices are coming back to me. My children, my children — the suffering is unbearable.”

Since February 2025, Bukavu has been controlled by M23 rebels. Congo’s government struggles to exert control over the east of the country, where more than 100 armed groups are vying for control of trillions of dollars in mineral wealth that’s critical for much of the world’s technology.

Health services are under severe strain as the region grapples with the deadliest Ebola outbreak in history that has killed more than 3,300 people, with more than 6,800 confirmed cases recorded.

Corneille Nangaa, leader of the political-military coalition Alliance Fleuve Congo, or AFC, which includes M23, promised measures to protect school children from future fires.

“It is true that many things happen here on earth by God’s will, for we are all pilgrims here; yet, many things also stem from idleness and our own human errors," he said at the funeral.

“As residents of Bukavu in particular — and of the DRC in general — let us resolve, starting today, to take a stand and make the decision to limit such damage through our own actions.”

___

Macklemore said Monday that he has been dropped from Ed Sheeran 's tour over pro-Palestinian comments made by the Grammy-winning rapper earlier this month onstage at New Jersey's MetLife Stadium.

Macklemore said on Instagram that several U.S. venues told the promoter they would prohibit him from performing as Sheeran's opening act for the Loop tour.

As a result, he wrote, Sheeran's team decided to remove him from the tour. That's despite the fact that the rapper — best known for his breakout hit “Thrift Shop” and the same-sex marriage anthem “Same Love” — has been making similar comments about the plight of Palestinians for years.

“So why is it an issue now? Because I’m sharing a stage with one of the biggest artists in the world, in some of the biggest stadiums in America,” Macklemore wrote. “At a certain level of exposure, ‘Free Palestine’ becomes too much of a risk.”

A growing chorus of organizations and experts say Israel’s wartime actions in Gaza amount to genocide — an accusation Israel vehemently rejects.

Sheeran has not commented and representatives for the singer did not immediately respond to emails seeking comment.

The promoter, Messina Touring Group, confirmed in a statement to Rolling Stone that it had been notified by venues that “they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans.”

Among the venues is Gillette Stadium, home to the NFL's New England Patriots. Owner Robert Kraft said the decision to cancel Macklemore was a result of his recent comments “and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community.”

“This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf. Their pain and loss are real,” Kraft said in a statement Monday.

Macklemore’s advocacy “should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas,” Kraft said.

The rapper, born Benjamin Hammond Haggerty in Washington state, exclaimed “Free Palestine” during the Sept. 5 date of the tour while introducing his protest song “Hind’s Hall.” Written following the 2024 campus protests in support of Palestinians, it's named for Hind Rajab, a 5-year-old Palestinian girl who was killed after Israeli forces fired on her family’s car in Gaza City.

“To all of my Jewish brothers and sisters, criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide, it in no way is criticism of you,” he said during the New Jersey concert. “This message is for peace, love, for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect, and equality.”

His comments drew criticism from fellow singer Pink, who herself then drew backlash.

Macklemore said he holds no ill will toward Sheeran, who he considers a friend.

“But as I told Ed multiple times on the phone, our friendship can’t change my responsibility to tell the truth about what happened,” Macklemore wrote.

The Loop Tour is scheduled to appear in venues including Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia; Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia; Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis; Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, North Carolina; AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas; and Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida.

News.title: Wall Street hit by tech sell-off after AI bosses push for slowdown
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Tech stocks have fallen sharply after Elon Musk and the boss of OpenAI joined calls for the slowdown of AI development. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Hundreds of hotels, pubs and restaurants urge Burnham to slash VAT | Prime Minister challenged to honour pledge to cut levy to 10pc and save thousands of jobs

2) Trump rejects Silicon Valley’s calls for AI slowdown | US president says ‘very negative forces’ are overstating the risks

3) Labour’s wealth raid ‘kills off ultra-luxury homes in London’ | A 120-home project in St John’s Wood is likely to be the last residence of its kind

4) Factories slash hiring ahead of Budget | Manufacturing vacancies fall by 6.2pc, despite rising business confidence

5) David Lloyd waters down net zero targets | Gym chain has spent millions on solar panels and heat pumps in effort to cut emissions

What happened overnight

Asian stocks fell as traders assessed fresh safety concerns over the pace of AI development.

South Korea’s Kospi lost 3.3pc to 6,679.23 and Japan’s Nikkei 225 index slid 0.6pc to 63,633.57. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 0.3pc to 24,886.81.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq index dropped 1.2pc in Asian trading hours, while S&P 500 futures shed 0.5pc. Those linked to The Dow Jones Industrial Average were down 0.1pc.

It came despite efforts from Donald Trump to downplay concerns about AI technology, saying on Sunday that “very negative forces” were overstating the risks.

On Saturday, Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei called for tech companies to slow down their advancement and for more work to be done on AI safety. His comments were backed by Sam Altman, the OpenAI boss, Sir Demis Hassabis, the chairman of Google DeepMind, and Elon Musk.

Oil rose after Saudi Arabia was forced to close a crucial oil pipeline after drone attacks from Iraq on Friday. Brent crude was up 2.8pc to $107.5 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate rose 2.22pc to $102.3 a barrel.

The US’s 10-year Treasury yields edged closer to the crucial 5pc level on Friday amid the prolonged bond sell-off, while two-year yields climbed to 4.66pc.

News.content:
All our reviewers are either resident destination experts or travel writers that specialise in hotels. Often they will have stayed at a hotel many times and so can see how it has changed for better or worse over the years. They know what makes a great hotel in that particular destination and will compare it contextually against local competition. When our reviewers first visit a hotel, they stay for at least one night, eat one meal in addition to breakfast and will experience all of the facilities on offer. Whichever category of room they stay in, they will see the entry-level rooms in order to assess them.



After their stay, our reviewers then give the hotel six scores out of 10, rating its location, style and character, service and facilities, rooms, food and drink, and value for money. The average of these scores then determines the overall score. News.title: Asia on high alert as El Niño threatens new Dengue epidemic
News.content:
Countries from Brazil to Taiwan are bracing for a surge in dengue driven by the “supersized” El Niño, as the UN warns this year’s weather phenomenon could be the strongest on record.

Both the virus and the Aedes mosquitoes that transmit it are especially sensitive to heat – and the El Niño is expected to push global temperatures to new highs.

“El Niño is being supersized before our eyes,” Antonio Guterres, the UN Secretary General, said last week. “The ​science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up.”

The weather phenomenon – a periodic warming of sea surface temperature in the eastern Pacific, caused by weakening trade winds – alters rainfall and temperature patterns across the globe. That, in turn, causes extreme weather like droughts, heatwaves, floods and typhoons – which then trigger events including wildfires, crop failures and a collapse in affected fisheries.

But it can also have a major impact on the transmission of disease, including dengue – and countries across the world, especially in Asia and Latin America, are bracing for outbreaks.

In July, Brazil’s Ministry of Health sent an alert warning states that arboviruses like dengue, chikungunya and Zika could surge later this year, and urged officials to ramp up disease surveillance and mosquito control programmes.

The increase will likely peak in 2027: the biomedical research institute Fiocruz has estimated that Brazil will see 1.7 million dengue cases next year, driven by El Niño.

News.title: ‘Your home is your palace’: Queen Elizabeth II’s housekeeper answers reader questions
News.content:
Was there one surprisingly simple trick used in the palace that made things feel instantly more polished?

Jay, West Midlands

Making sure you have a routine is the best way for everything to feel polished. At the palace, the team is trained, and everyone has the right tools and time to do their job... They learned how to lift things safely and how to be confident when they were around the Royal Collection. When you’re cleaning historic areas such as palaces and castles, you have to make sure you don’t overdo it. We had a daily routine that ensured we didn’t over-clean everything.

What is the royal protocol for dealing with ironing and maintaining perfectly crisp sheets without using harsh, eco-unfriendly chemicals?

Saleem, London

Much of what would be classed as royal protocol are things we would do in our own homes. For linen, you need to treat it well and look after it by not washing it at too high a temperature or using too much detergent. Make sure the products you’re using are eco-friendly, not only for the environment, but also to care for the linen. For historic linen, it needs to be handled very gently, as it can tear quite easily.

Did the Queen get involved in any of the details of housekeeping?

Peter, East of England

I was very blessed. The Queen did leave it up to me to make those decisions because she trusted me to keep her home and the other royal residences clean and up to a great standard. I kept in touch with her, making sure the team was involved. We would have regular update meetings to ensure everyone knew what was happening and when. There was planned cleaning throughout the year depending on what was occurring, making sure certain areas were protected or closed off, for example.

I would feel very stressed cleaning around objects of great value, history and sentiment. How do you avoid disasters?

Catherine, North West

It’s important the team feels confident when cleaning those areas. We achieve that through training and building their confidence.

In the castle, we introduced a cleaning schedule that covered different areas within the state apartments – and it meant that we didn’t over-clean. The structure of this schedule was important. Every day, we would ensure we vacuumed and damp-dusted; there were no actual chemicals or any what I call “wet chemicals”. On a Monday, for instance, we would clean vases. On a Tuesday, we would do the fireplaces. On a Wednesday, it would be light fittings.

It’s crucial the team is given the right amount of time to clean, so that they don’t feel rushed or stressed. But we also have to remember that accidents happen. And if an accident happens and it was just an accident, then what can you do? It’s just one of those things.

Ultimately, making sure people are trained and confident is the key.

With limited time, what are the housekeeping priorities?

David, South West

My housekeeping priorities when at home are to make things look really tidy quickly. Putting your newspapers away, fluffing the cushions up, tidying the curtains, making sure your washing is cleared and the dishwasher is on – these are all things that will make a big difference, even if you haven’t had time to get your mop or vacuum out.

When are you satisfied a room is clean?

D, North West

I am quite a hard taskmaster and I do like perfection, but equally, that comes with making sure people understand the guidelines and what’s expected of them, after being trained properly.

I like to be visible and around the team, showing them what I’m looking at. I would get them to sit on a toilet and then shut the door, so they could see what’s behind the door – or sit in the bath, because that way you can see what other people are seeing when they’re using it. If you’re cleaning and rushing around, you don’t always see those little details.

News.title: Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure
News.content:
Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

News.title: Redemption Sunday for Hull and Woad as Europe reclaim Solheim Cup
News.content:
The quiet but steely 22-year-old, who everyone seemed to have forgotten was a rookie, punched her fist when she held the decisive two-footer, before the customary hug with opponent Auston Kim and then being mobbed by her team.

“This was really important,” Woad said. “I mean, I was pretty disappointed and felt like I was kind of letting everyone down. Then the captain kind of spoke to me and said that I was third on [the most] birdies [made]. So I just had to trust that and that’s golf sometimes. And it ended up I got the winning putt.”

Some will claim that Woad was only the match-winner on a technicality. Carlota Ciganda in the penultimate game had not finished off her win against Jennifer Kupcho, but when Woad tapped in, the Spaniard was three up with three to go and was guaranteed a half. So the acclaim Woad received was granted. Not that anyone in the Europe camp cared.

The previous evening they had returned to their team room feeling slightly down that they did not hold the advantage, Kupcho holing a 91-footer on the 17th and a 30-footer on the 18th to deny Ciganda and Céline Boutier. And their mood was not helped when videos appeared on social media of the Americans taking crates of beer on to the bus back to their hotel. Yet that foolish scenario only offered extra incentive. “At least we’ll be the ones taking crates of beer on to our bus this evening,” Mel Reid, the assistant captain, said quite pointedly.

News.title: Lando Norris fumes at virtual safety car rules for costing him Spanish GP win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix, the first time the race has been held at the all-new, purpose-built street circuit, the Madring. The track has developed a reputation in its short life for being a bit of a tricky one. Some have gone so far as to call it a “car killer”? Is it living up to that reputation? Probably, especially if you look at some of the lower formulae that have run on it.

It has also increasingly become the case for the Formula One cars, too. The first couple of practice sessions on Friday revealed little to worry about. As the drivers began to push, though, from final practice and qualifying, the mistakes and crashes happened. The biggest so far was Oliver Bearman but also a smaller one for Lewis Hamilton.

There will almost certainly be some kind of incident in the race, but whether we see red flags, safety cars and so on remains to be seen. A bigger and perhaps more significant question will be how much overtaking will take place on this track. The drivers are not optimistic. The theory goes that if tyre degradation is high then there will be, because you will have significant pace offsets between worn and fresh tyres. The problem is that the leaders tend not to differ to greatly from one another on strategy these days...

Perhaps George Russell, who qualified down in sixth and has little to lose, will be brave and put on a set of hard tyres to start with. Russell has work to do yet again. He was not miles off Antonelli in qualifying when it came to pace, but given how close it was in the top six, finds four cars between himself and the championship leader, who just missed out on pole to McLaren’s Lando Norris.

Norris said it was the best lap of his life and seemed to come from nowhere. He improved more than a second from Q2 to Q3 and continues his fine form in 2026. He will start alongside Antonelli with Max Verstappen in third, Lewis Hamilton in fourth and Charles Leclerc in fifth, before Russell.

News.title: Tora Bora’s last midwife struggles under Taliban rule as aid runs dry
News.content:
The small clinic, crowded with pregnant women, sits in the shadow of Tora Bora in eastern Afghanistan. Twenty-five years ago, those mountains commanded the attention of the world’s most powerful military. Roughly 15 miles from the clinic, in the Tora Bora cave complex, Osama bin Laden was believed to be hiding as American bombs rained down in the hunt for the architect of 9/11.

Today, another consequence of the West’s long entanglement with Afghanistan is playing out beneath those same mountains – in the struggle to keep mothers and babies alive.

In the baking courtyard of Gandab Kharoti health centre, dozens of women enveloped in sapphire blue burqas sit shoulder to shoulder beneath trees waiting to see Shila Ibrahimi, a 27-year-old midwife.

The women rest against walls, dusty, barefoot children play, and mothers cradle sick babies beneath folds of cloth. Some have walked for hours through the mountains to reach her.

Among them is Fawzia, 30, seven-and-a-half months pregnant with her seventh child. Suffering from headaches, she has walked for miles through the heat.

Her husband works far from the village, so she makes the journey with her children and mother-in-law, hoping the Taliban do not stop her for the crime of travelling without a male escort.

Under the Taliban’s morality rules, women face restrictions on travelling alone, while UN monitors have documented the regime’s morality inspectors ordering some health facilities not to treat unaccompanied women.

But enforcement varies and Fawzia says nobody challenged her on her journey here. Asked where she would give birth if the clinic closed she says: “We have nowhere else to go. We cannot afford that. We are poor.”

Sports.title: Howard Webb set to give public explanation in next 24 hours for astonishing VAR blunder over Haaland goal at Man Utd
Sports.content:
REFS’ chief Howard Webb is set to explain tonight how the staggering Old Trafford VAR blunder unfolded.

Video ref Matt Donohue and assistant Blake Antrobus paid the price for their howler with both dropped from duties.



And while Manchester United do not plan to take it any further after Erling Haaland’s City derby winner, Pro Ref leader Webb is expected to go through the entire incident in front of TV cameras.

Haaland’s second-half goal – with Pro Ref conceding it should have been ruled out for offside against Enzo Fernandez – is due to be the focal point of the first edition of this season’s Match Officials Mic’d Up show.



Webb will be able to play out the communication between Donohue and Antrobus in the Stockley Park video booth before Michael Oliver was told to signal the goal for City.

Oliver recognised the scale of the mistake, apparent to Pro Ref bosses almost as soon as the goal was awarded.



Webb gave the green light for Pro Ref to make a public admission of the “error of judgement” within three hours of the final whistle on Sunday.

He is now set to lay out the procedural cock-ups that were made and give an indication of the steps that will be adopted to prevent a repeat.

Sports.title: Richarlison gives pointed response after De Zerbi says he will not play for Tottenham even if he’s fit
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM outcast Richarlison issued a cryptic response after manager Roberto De Zerbi stated he will not play for his team, even if he’s fit.

The winger failed to find a new club during the summer transfer window and has ended up in limbo.



Transfer insider Fabrizio Romano shared a quote from De Zerbi, 47, saying the Brazil international is not part of his plans.

It read: “Richarlison will not play even if he’s available. Not even in the Carabao Cup, no.”



And Richarlison responded in the comments’ section with a simple crying emoji.

This comes after the 29-year-old was left out of Tottenham’s squad for Tuesday’s trip to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup’s third round.

The exiled Brazilian has also been omitted from Spurs’ 25-man squad for the Premier League after asking to leave.

De Zerbi said: “Richarlison, you already know everything and nothing changed for Carabao Cup or Premier League. The situation is the same.

Asked if that meant the ex-Everton man would not be involved at Anfield, the Italian simply replied: “No.”

De Zerbi added: “I stay in the middle and I can’t say nothing more because it is not my job. I can answer about the result and the players in the squad, the offensive phase, the defensive phase, but not for other things.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“What I have done at the beginning of this season has been to speak with him and to propose an extension of the contract. If he said, ‘No thank you,’ I finished my job.

“I said in the last press conference. I know what happened in the last 45 days. It’s not right if I explained. It’s not my behaviour. The relationship, the problem is between the player and the club.

“I stay within the club. It’s coach and club together. At the start of this season I spoke to him many times to convince him to stay and he didn’t want to. I can’t go every day to pray for him to stay.”

Hours after the press conference, Richarlison posted on Instagram stories a screengrab of De Zerbi’s quote confirming his exclusion for the cup, coupled with his own comment of “Why?” and a sad emoji face.

The ex-Brighton manager revealed last month “Richie” had asked to leave in the summer and snubbed a contract extension, with his current deal running out in June.



Thus, Spurs didn’t include the forward in their Premier League squad – despite him registering 11 goals and four assists in 32 Prem appearances last term – and attempted to sell him.

But moves to Everton, Trabzonspor and Vasco da Gama all fell through over personal terms.

And now there is a good chance Richarlison will be stuck at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium until at least January.

Meanwhile, Sandro Tonali is out of the Liverpool game having picked up a knock.

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star tipped for stardom by Wenger waited 12 YEARS for first Premier League goal – now he can shock Gunners
Sports.content:
CHUBA AKPOM was once tipped to be Arsenal’s main man, now he is in line to play against the Gunners after a rollercoaster journey.

Akpom, now 30, could feature against Arsenal on Tuesday when Ipswich host Mikel Arteta’s side in the League Cup third round.



The experienced striker has taken the scenic route to return to the Premier League with Ipswich this season.

His goal against Manchester United last month was his first in the Prem, coming 12 years and 350 days after Arsene Wenger handed him his debut for Arsenal as a 17-year-old.



That remarkable wait means he has the third-longest gap between debut and first goal in Prem history, behind only Damien Delany and Jack Robinson.

And it is the perfect illustration of Akpom’s unconventional career to date, a journey that has seen him play across 12 different teams in five different countries.

Akpom was always amongst the highest-rated youngsters in Arsenal’s academy, earning a stellar reputation when he was picked up aged just six from Rippleway FC after scoring over 100 goals in just two seasons.

Former Arsenal Under-21 boss and Head of Academy Coaching Terry Burton remembers expectations always being high for Akpom, from both the staff and the fans.

He told SunSport: “I think he always had that when he was coming through the academy.

“There were always people talking about Chuba, he was always held up to be a potential star player.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Sometimes at a younger age you don’t realise that it’s not enough to have people saying it, you have got to actually do it and achieve it.”

Akpom was a regular fixture of the England youth setup too, given his enormous potential, and Under-19s boss Noel Blake reckons his qualities are the same today as they were back then.

Blake told SunSport: “What you see with Chuba now, you saw it then. His shape hasn’t changed, his physicality and his stature.

“But his feet were frightening. He had excellent feet. He could play as a striker as a No10 and in the pockets.”



But despite such incredible promise, Akpom never managed to break into the Arsenal first team.

He left in 2018 after making just 12 appearances and spending most of his time on loan at Brentford, Coventry, Nottingham Forest, Hull, Brighton and Belgian side Sint-Truiden.

You would be forgiven for thinking a move to the lower leagues was on the cards, but Akpom opted for a rarely-trodden path – joining Greek top-flight side PAOK.

Aged 22 at the time, Akpom helped PAOK to an unbeaten league campaign with six goals – including a crucial winner against title rivals Olympiacos.



And he topped it off with an overhead kick to win the Greek Cup final and turn an invincible season into a double.

Akpom’s former PAOK team-mate, Omar El Kaddouri, told SunSport: “It was the perfect step for him. We were playing in Europe so he could show himself to the whole of Europe.

“Not a lot of people knew of him outside of England and I think PAOK was the perfect step for him. He got better, he improved a lot.”

Akpom would watch Arsenal games on the team bus and support his former club from a distance in Greece, keeping a special place in his heart for the team that first gave him a chance.



But when the opportunity to return to England came, it was Middlesbrough who came knocking.

The striker joined Boro in 2020, and after two seasons of struggle in the Championship, Akpom was on the brink of leaving the club after being made to train with the U21s by boss Chris Wilder.

That all changed when Michael Carrick came in to replace Wilder and Akpom thrived, winning the Championship Golden Boot with 28 goals in 38 games.

A £12m move to Ajax followed, where Akpom spent two seasons and scored 23 goals before securing another European adventure in a switch to French club Lille on loan.

But it was last season when the lure of England crept back in and Akpom joined Ipswich on loan with a view to making the deal permanent this summer.



Now, after his remarkable journey, he finds himself facing the club where it all started.

Former England youth boss Blake said: “Ask any England coach at that time, they will tell you Chuba always had a terrific attitude.

“He was determined. He has great strength of character, a great resilience and he was determined to achieve something in the game.



“Whatever that may look like. He definitely had ability, resilience and a willingness to win.”

That willingness to win may have seen him regularly fighting team-mates in training while in Greece, but it is also the reason he is now taking on Arsenal back in England.

El Kaddouri added: “It is going to be emotional for him. It is his team. When he was playing for PAOK he used to follow them, watch their games and cheer for them.

“It is a special club for him and it is always special to play the team where you grew up. I am sure he will still be trying to score.

“I have played with some of the best players in the world, like Gonzalo Higuain, Marek Hamsik and Edinson Cavani.



“The biggest difference between them and others is being competitive and wanting to win even in training and being competitive all the time. Chuba has that.”

Sports.title: Chelsea loanees suffer nightmare week as calls grow for wonderkid, 19, to be recalled from Champions League side
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’s loan army were a mixed bag this week, despite NONE of their ones to watch actually winning a game.

Only Benoit Badiashile’s Napoli earned a victory, but he did not play any part in it.



SunSport is keeping a keen eye on the Blues’ best or most promising loanees this season.

In this week’s Loan Watch, we have rounded up the performances of their most promising youngsters and experienced stars who could be sold.



Fans are calling for one of Chelsea’s most exciting attacking prospects to be recalled over a lack of minutes.

And it was a nightmare week for Axel Disasi at Crystal Palace – although his team-mate seems to have a bright future at Stamford Bridge.



This is how the best of the Blues loanees got on last week…

Ryan Kavuma-McQueen

Ryan Kavuma-McQueen’s late Championship cameo for Portsmouth brought a much-needed spark to the goalless draw at Charlton.

But the 17-year-old Chelsea loanee had only 17 minutes to make a difference.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The patient winger nearly found a winner with a box-office ball across goal that came within inches of a Colby Bishop finish.



Kavuma-McQueen sent a rocket from way out that flew just over the bar, but the final whistle blew with the youngster storming down the wing.

Mheuka was subbed on in the 77th minute, with Celtic already losing 3-0 to Rangers in a Scottish Cup edition of the Old Firm derby.

Genesis Antwi and Filip Jorgensen have been thoroughly impressive since joining Strasbourg on loan, drawing 1-1 with Monaco on Saturday.

He had a nightmare last week, and this week was an unused substitute in a 1-0 win for his side against Bologna.

The French defender received a red card just 34 minutes into Crystal Palace’s 3-2 defeat to Ipswich.

Reggie Walsh played 70 minutes in Wigan’s 0-0 draw with Sheffield Wednesday.

He also came close from 25 yards out and was strong again in a good performance against the third-tier leaders.

He is being kept out of the team by the impressive performances of Jean Butez in net, with Como having the chance to go top of Serie A tonight.

Mamadou Sarr – Real Sociedad

Mamadou Sarr played the full match against Atletico Madrid, which is good — but the game ended 3-0 to Diego Simeone’s side.



Despite the result, Sarr was solid.

He completed the most passes of anyone on the pitch and was strong in his duels.

By the 80th minute, he was a genuine contender to be man of the match.

Three goals after the 84th minute made sure that would not be the case, but the result is certainly misleading.

And with Chelsea’s defensive woes, a good season could see him brought into their plans sooner rather than later.

Sports.title: How controversial Haaland decision at Man Utd unfolded with Pro Ref chiefs realising major blunder almost immediately
Sports.content:
IT was the VAR decision that left the whole of football perplexed.

When Erling Haaland netted from close range in the Manchester derby, the flag seemed a simple and correct decision.



Nearly three minutes later, to disbelief inside and outside Old Trafford, the goal was awarded.

Sun Sport explains how it all transpired:



5.47pm: Erling Haaland gets on the end of Josko Gvardiol’s deflected cross to turn the ball past Senne Lammens but even as he turned away towards the travelling Manchester City fans, the flag was raised, with referee Michael Oliver signalling a free-kick and confirmed to VAR Matt Donohue: “The on-field decision is offside, Erling Haaland.”

Donohue and the video team at Stockley Park begin the checks, with the expectation that the offside call would be confirmed, with the replay operator rolling back the tape.

5.48pm: As Matt Donohue looks at the replay images from the side-on camera it becomes clear that the call is closer than it had initially seemed, especially as the 18-yard camera at Old Trafford is offset from the straight line.

Hawkeye replay operators confirm the decision is tight, meaning Donohue and his colleagues turn to the Semi-Automated Offside Technology tracking cameras supplied by Genius Sports – who sit in an adjacent booth. The cameras track thousands of data points per players every second.

When SAOT suggests Erling Haaland was fractionally onside – although not within the 5cm “tolerance” zone used to give attackers an advantage – Donohue and his assistant still need to check the calibration and kick point of Josko Gvardiol’s cross are accurate.

Haaland, it is confirmed, was onside, with the computerised animated illustration to explain the decision now being generated.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

5.49pm: With Michael Oliver explaining to the players of both sides that the check is continuing – amid moans from fans about the delay in confirming an “obvious” call – Matt Donohue’s attention turns to Enzo Fernandez in the middle of the goal.

It appears that Donohue’s sole focus, while accepting Fernandez was in an offside position, was whether he touched the ball with his diving header.

Once again, SAOT is used, determining that there was no contact – which would have meant Erling Haaland was ALSO offside when he turned the ball home.

But this was where it all went wrong.



Donohue needed to also look at the wider context of Fernandez’s action, which saw Lisandro Martinez drawn towards him and keeper Senne Lammens unable to react until the ball had gone past the Manchester City midfielder.

At that point, he should have told Oliver that while Haaland was onside, it was felt that Fernandez was “interfering” with the Manchester United defender and keeper and that the referee was being advised to visit the pitchside monitor with a recommendation of ruling a “subjective” offside and no goal.

5.50pm: Instead, Michael Oliver was merely told that there was no offside offence, and “you can award the goal”. Cue Manchester City joy and Manchester United fury.

5.51pm: Soon after the final decision, it was clear to Pro Ref chiefs at Stockley Park that a huge mistake had been made. But with Manchester United having kicked off, there was now nothing anyone could do to change the error.

Sports.title: Shearer brands Bruno Fernandes ‘pathetic’ as ex-Premier League star says Haaland goal was ‘karma’ for Man Utd captain
Sports.content:
ALAN SHEARER has slammed “pathetic” Bruno Fernandes after the Manchester United captain sparked Phil Foden’s derby red.

Fernandes’ United were beaten 1-0 by bitter rivals Manchester City at Old Trafford on Sunday thanks to a dodgy VAR-given winner by Erling Haaland.



And the loss was all-the-more gutting for the Red side of Manchester after Foden had been sent off in just the 23rd minute.

Foden, 26, saw red after thrusting his studs into Fernandes’ stomach havig been grounded in a tussle between the pair.



But cameras showed Fernandes, 32, aim a couple of sneaky kicks at the prostrate England star before he lashed out.

And Premier League record-scorer Shearer was far from impressed with Fernandes’ actions, or referee Michael Oliver.

The Newcastle legend said on The Rest Is Football: “I thought the way Bruno Fernandes went down was pathetic.

“He helped get Foden off and, yes, he’s kicked out at him a little bit but Bruno Fernandes has also kicked Phil Foden.

“If Phil Foden reacts in the same way as Bruno Fernandes did then both get red cards. So, for me, either both are red or neither of them are.

“He’s kicked out, so he’s stupid, OK? But Bruno Fernandes has done the same thing so for me, without doubt, they both should’ve been a red card if Michael Oliver thinks Phil Foden’s is a red card.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Aston Villa legend Gabby Agbonlahor agreed with Shearer.

And he believes Haaland’s controversial winner was “karma” for United.

The Man City superstar hit the back of the net in the hourmark after a long VAR check that overruled Oliver’s offside decision.

The semi-automated offside technology proved Haaland, 26, was covered by Patrick Dorgu but VAR missed the fact Enzo Fernandez interfered in the build-up from an offside position.

Pro Ref – the official refereeing body in England – publicly admitted that was the wrong decision and apologised to the Red Devils.



However, Agbonlahor believes that was justice following Foden’s red card.

The former England international told talkSPORT: “At the end of the day, Bruno Fernandes is a cheat. He’s an outstanding player, but he’s a cheat.

“You’ve kicked Foden twice on the floor, which should have been a red card to you.



“Then Foden’s lashed out a tiny little bit and you’re rolling around when you’re not hurt.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“A proper referee goes over and says: ‘You two, cut it out, a yellow each, play on’. It’s never a red card.

“That’s why you get your karma. Maybe the goal that should’ve been disallowed on Haaland, is the karma you sometimes get in football for the red card to Phil Foden.”

Sports.title: ‘Least I could do’ – England star Ollie Watkins’ heartwarming gesture revealed before £50million Saudi transfer
Sports.content:
OLLIE WATKINS surprised fans as he chipped in a stunning £5,000 to help a six-year-old’s children’s hospital fundraiser.

The former Aston Villa striker spotted the appeal from the Key Stage One kid on socials, where Albie Egan asked Watkins for a hand in helping out Birmingham Children’s Hospital.



Watkins, who made the £51million move from Villa to Saudi club Al-Hilal this summer, admitted it was the “least he could do”.

Albie took on a the huge challenge to move 31 miles in 31 days and he smashed it.



The Cannock boy covered a whopping 40 miles in total and has raised £8,607 on JustGiving for the hospital charity so far.

That is 17,214 per cent of the original target.



And Watkins’ £5,000 donation will become £6,250 with Gift Aid.

On his donation note, he wrote: “Albie I saw your video, well done mate.

“Good luck you should be proud of yourself! Hope this donation helps. Like you said it’s the least I could do! Ollie.”

Before Watkins got involved, Albie had raised around £3,000.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

But the Birmingham Children’s Hospital is not just any charity to Albie.

Albie was previously looked after by the staff at the hospital after the Egan’s discovered he needed a bone cyst removing.

Speaking to the Express & Star, dad David Egan was bursting with pride for his son.

He said: “He’s made so much effort and he’s smashed it. Honestly, he’s done amazing.”

In the viral video on David’s X, Albie said: “I’m really sad about this, Ollie Watkins.



“For every year I’ve had a Villa shirt, and on my sixth year this was the first ever year that I decided I want my favourite player, and you’ll never guess who it was.

“It’s you! And the least you could do is raise money for Birmingham Children’s Hospital.”

And since learning of the massive donation, Albie’s love for his favourite player has only grown.

When he saw the donation, he cheered: “Oh my God! This is so amazing Ollie Watkins, oh my god, I’m so excited.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“You know what, I’m keeping it on the back [the Ollie Watkins name].



“It has made my entire life.”

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher sticks the boot in on Bruno Fernandes over 'disappointing' antics in Man City loss
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher sticks the boot in on Bruno Fernandes over 'disappointing' antics in Man City loss

Jamie Carragher says he was "really disappointed" with the actions of Bruno Fernandes during the incident which led to Phil Foden's red card in the loss against Manchester City

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher was not impressed with Bruno Fernandes (Image: Sky Sports)

Jamie Carragher has condemned the behaviour of Bruno Fernandes following the incident that led to Phil Foden being sent off in the Manchester derby.

‌



The Manchester City midfielder was shown a straight red card after aiming a kick at the midriff of Fernandes, who had left Foden on the ground following a coming together by the touchline. The Manchester United captain then sent his foot into the small of Foden's back, sparking the violent reaction which curtailed his involvement in the game.

‌



Erling Haaland went on to win the game for City following a highly dubious VAR intervention which, along with Foden's red card, became one of the major talking points from the derby.

‌



Fernandes escaped punishment for his part in the clash with Foden and Carragher has now questioned the Portugal international for the manner of his reaction after the 'kick'.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“What I would say is two yellows [cards] would have been fine. But I was really disappointed with Bruno Fernandes,” Carragher said on Monday Night Football.

“There’s a lot of things in football that we like or we don’t like. My big one that I really don’t like is people going down, pretending they’re hurt. But doing that…I can’t have it.

“I know there will be Manchester United fans watching this saying: “Oh it’s because he’s a Manchester United player, it’s because he’s a foreign player”. On this show about five or six years ago Harry Kane did the same in a game between Tottenham and Everton and I said the same, I can’t accept it. I’m not having the reaction from Bruno there, it was a brush from his foot.”

‌



View 2 Images Fernandes was kicked by Foden during the derby (Image: Shaun Brooks/Getty Images)

Roy Keane echoed similar sentiments when he dissected the incident at half-time of Sunday's game on Sky Sports.

“Foden gets up and reacts obviously so he's now sent off. The strange thing is, if you look at it, so Bruno catches him, gives the foul away and gives him a little kick. Foden is sent off and I'm guessing it's classed as violent conduct.

Article continues below

“To me, Bruno is the one who's violent here. I have to call it out. I called Kyle Walker out a few years ago when he went down with a headbutt. Listen, we see violence, I suppose, in a different way. But I don't think that's a red card for Foden.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta compared to Sir Alex Ferguson after Arsenal take drastic referee action
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta compared to Sir Alex Ferguson after Arsenal take drastic referee action

Arsenal secured their fourth win from as many Premier League games against Sunderland but Mikel Arteta was left furious with a refereeing decision after the game

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta was fuming after Sunderland were awarded a controversial penalty against Sunderland (Image: (David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Jamie Carragher has branded Mikel Arteta 'the Sir Alex Ferguson' of the modern Premier League era after the Arsenal boss described the penalty given against his side as 'not acceptable'. The Gunners might have maintained their perfect start to the season with a hard-fought 2-0 victory over Sunderland on Saturday night, but the Spaniard was left furious by the penalty decision that went against his team.

‌



A dramatic second-half saw referee John Brooks point to the spot when Dan Ballard was brought down by Ezri Konsa, and David Raya parried Enzo Le Fee’s subsequent effort onto the left post. But that didn’t stop Arteta from fuming about the decision in his post-match press conference.

‌



Former United boss Ferguson would always make his feelings known on decisions that went against his side during his time in charge at Old Trafford, and Carragher, speaking on Monday Night Football, believes Arteta came across in the same way as the Scot once did. He said: “This was Mikel Arteta becoming the Alex Ferguson of the Premier League right now.

‌



“He’s the 'Don' at the moment and the Premier League champion. There are a lot of new managers about, he’s been in his role for six or seven years and he feels he is in a position of power to say it wasn’t a penalty and I don’t think it was a penalty.

“But it will be interesting to see how long it takes for another referee to give a penalty against Arsenal in a similar situation.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“But I thought it was very interesting in the press conference, one of the journalists made a point about no matter what question you asked him he kept going back to the penalty.

“He was determined to get the narrative out that this won’t happen again to his club, but listen that is management. We have seen it with Alex Ferguson, with Jose Mourinho.”

‌



Agreeing with Carragher, former Luton Town and Wolves boss Rob Edwards said: “I think Jamie is right, he is putting himself in a position where he is looking after his team and football club and people will listen to a Premier League winning manager. They will listen as he is a powerful voice there.”

On the penalty decision, Edwards said: “We don’t want to see the crappling or the pulling for long periods, but I don’t think it is (a penalty), Dave (Jones), I’m sorry.

View 3 Images Arsenal were furious after conceding a penalty during their win over Sunderland

‌



“You can see the grab from the angle we are going to get in a second but, I think Dan Ballard knows what he is doing and he pulls Konsa with him. I don’t think it is a penalty.”

Mirror Football reported on Monday that Arsenal have made contact with Howard Webb, Pro Ref’s chief refereeing officer, as they want an explanation about why the decision was given by Brooks. And w hen asked for his thoughts on the decision on Saturday night, Arteta fumed: “The first question and we have to discuss this.

"This is not acceptable at this level because it was a beautiful game of football with two teams, with an atmosphere in the stadium (that) was unbelievable. Sunderland they are so organised, so good in so many phases, they have great players and they create a lot of issues.

‌



View 3 Images Sir Alex Ferguson was known for his forthright views on refereeing decisions (Image: John Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images)

“We had to cope with all of that because it was a lot and a really difficult win after Chelsea and Napoli. On top of that we have to go through what we’ve done today that, in my opinion, is not acceptable.

“I watched it 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how they’d think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. I don’t know what to think really. I’m sad we have to discuss before the game something at this level that has the gravity of that.

Article continues below

“That changes the course of the season and it can cost you the Champions League. At this level, with all the work we put in, this cannot happen.”

Sports.title: Howard Webb under growing pressure after Man Utd apology and Arsenal complaint
Sports.content:
Howard Webb under growing pressure after Man Utd apology and Arsenal complaint

Several Premier League clubs have major concerns over refereeing mistakes after another weekend of controversial decisions, most notably in the Manchester derby

View 3 Images Pro Ref chief Howard Webb is under pressure

Referees' chief Howard Webb is under mounting pressure after another huge blunder from his officials.

‌



Webb, Pro Ref’s chief refereeing officer, has axed the VAR team Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus from next weekend’s Premier League fixtures after allowing Erling Haaland's winner to stand in the Manchester derby.

‌



Pro Ref have already been forced to contact Manchester United to explain the “error of judgment” as they failed to disallow City striker Haaland’s goal despite Enzo Fernandez being in an offside position and interfering with play.

‌



Arsenal have also made contact with Webb following Mikel Arteta ’s post-match rant that a penalty was given against Ezri Konsa for a challenge on Sunderland's Dan Ballard.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



It is understood Arsenal want an explanation about why the decision was given by referee John Brooks.

Referees are under orders to clamp down on penalty box grappling but Arsenal may feel they have been unfairly targeted because similar incidents went unpunished in other games.

It has left Webb feeling the heat and Mirror Sport understands that several clubs have major concerns about consistency, new directives - like grappling this season - not being applied fairly and why huge mistakes continue to happen.

‌



Webb has been in there job for coming up to four years and, while there is an acceptance that he is determined to drive change and they like his communication, there is frustration about refereeing standards.

View 3 Images Arsenal were furious after conceding a penalty during their win over Sunderland

United defender Lisandro Martinez described Haaland’s goal as an “injustice” because he and teammate, keeper Senne Lammens, were influenced by Fernandez’s presence.

‌



It has caused disbelief in football circles and the Haaland howler was compared to former Liverpool striker Luis Diaz’s goal being wrongly disallowed at Tottenham in 2023 which is widely regarded as the biggest blunder in VAR history.

Donohue and Antrobus have been stood down but Webb has got some explaining to do to clubs in the next Premier League shareholders’ meeting and also the next edition of Match Officials Mic’D Up.

View 3 Images Michael Oliver appears to have been absolved of blame (Image: Getty Images)

‌



But referee Michael Oliver, who was in charge at Old Trafford, is down to officiate Sunday’s match between Bournemouth and Liverpool so it would appear that he has been absolved of blame.

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher says the officials “lost focus” and that is why they did not give an offside rather than a goal. Gallagher told Sky: “I think they are so focused on whether Fernandez touches the ball - he doesn’t - that they’ve lost focus.

“He’s clearly gone to head the ball. If you watch, Lammens is the first affected because he goes to make the save, Martinez is dragged away from Haaland because he’s got to go to it.”

Sports.title: Four Man Utd players destroyed after painful Man City loss - 'They're walking'
Sports.content:
Four Man Utd players destroyed after painful Man City loss - 'They're walking'

Manchester United were beaten 1-0 by Man City in the Premier League on Sunday, with the Red Devils failing to take advantage of their opponents playing with 10 men for 67 minutes

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford and Bryan Mbeumo were among the Manchester United players criticised by Jaap Stam (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United legend Jaap Stam has criticised Bruno Fernandes, Marcus Rashford, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha following Sunday's derby defeat to Manchester City. The Red Devils suffered a 1-0 loss at home to their fierce rivals despite facing 10 men for 67 minutes plus added time.

‌



United boss Michael Carrick has now presided over the club's joint-worst opening to a Premier League season, matching last term's poor beginning under Ruben Amorim and the 1992-93 campaign. Carrick took over from the dismissed Portuguese manager on a temporary basis in January and delivered an impressive recovery that secured a third-place finish.

‌



However, United's sluggish opening has placed the former midfielder under increased pressure after being given the role permanently in May. Carrick's side languish in 13th position after four matches, a sequence that has featured defeat at Hull City and a frustrating stalemate at Everton.

‌



Now, former United centre-half Stam has delivered a scatching verdict on United and their players. He told Viaplay: "If you look at City and if you look at this game, it was easy for them today, even with 10 men.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"I was asking myself as well: the United team coming off the pitch, what are they thinking? Would they be thinking they've done everything that they can Is that it?

"Even in playing it out from the back, it was easy, one-two, keep the ball a little bit longer at your feet, somebody else is taking up different positions. You play it, make a little one-two, you're out and they can go and attack.

"Against 10 men, even if it's City with the quality that they have, you would expect United to be on the front foot every time, to be very, very aggressive, even the strikers tracking back. Then, of course, and that's a very important thing as well.

‌



"If you have possession and they are dropping a little bit deeper, use the side, use the width of the game a little bit, put crosses in the box. But now sometimes, you feel like when they're playing, there's not a real idea in how to get to opportunities and how to make it difficult for the opposition to score goals."

View 2 Images Jaap Stam has had his say on United's derby defeat (Image: Vince Mignott/MB Media/Getty Images)

City's winner at Old Trafford sparked controversy after Erling Haaland's goal stood despite Enzo Fernandez appearing to interfere with play while in an offside position. The Premier League's refereeing body Pro Ref has since acknowledged an "error of judgment" from the VAR officials.

‌



However, reviewing the build-up to Haaland's second-half strike, Stam highlighted what he saw as a worrying lack of urgency from United's forwards in getting back to support their teammates.

He added: "It's a long ball, they win it, City takes over and look at the front four [of United]. They're just walking, they're just looking at the situation,' the Dutchman added.

"A team that really wants to win, the strikers, it's about all the 11, it's about chasing. Against 10 men, it's about tracking back, it's about winning battles.

Article continues below

"From then on, you keep possession, you go out in transition and then you try to create and score goals."

Sports.title: Harry Maguire called VAR who allowed Erling Haaland goal a 'f****** joke'
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire called VAR who allowed Erling Haaland goal a 'f****** joke'

Manchester United were left feeling hard done by after a controversial VAR call at the weekend and one of the officials involved was in Harry Maguire's bad books earlier this year

View 3 Images Erling Haaland's winning goal in the Manchester derby was given by VAR (Image: Getty)

Manchester United were left furious this weekend when VAR intervened to allow an offside goal scored by Erling Haaland to stand, costing them victory in the Manchester derby.

Matt Donohue, the VAR official from the game, and his assistant have since been stood down from duty this weekend by Pro Ref, who issued an apology to United after Enzo Fernandez was ruled to have not played the ball despite attempting to reach Josko Gvardiol's cross while in an offside position.

As the fallout from Sunday's derby continues, a previous outburst from Harry Maguire directed at Donohue has resurfaced.

Back in March, he and his colleagues were branded a "f****** joke" by the central defender while operating as fourth official in Manchester United's 2-2 draw away at Bournemouth.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Maguire was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity on the south coast. Bournemouth were awarded a penalty for the offence with Maguire deemed to have pulled down Evanilson inside the penalty area.

That outburst earned Maguire an additional one match ban after Donohue shared the offensive remarks with an independent regulatory commission, claiming that Maguire said them as he left the field.

View 3 Images Harry Maguire was furious at the match officials, including Matt Donohue, after being sent off vs Bournemouth back in March (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Haaland's goal was originally ruled offside, only for VAR to intervene and overturn the decision. It quickly sparked a huge debate online with numerous pundits, including Gary Neville and Wayne Rooney, suggesting the VAR officials had got the call wrong.

An apology was issued just hours after the game, which Manchester City won 1-0. It read: "Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday's Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland's awarded goal.

"The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland - that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

View 3 Images Donahue has been stood down from duty this weekend (Image: Alex Dodd/CameraSport)

"In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

"Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place."

Sports.title: Man Utd VAR stood down after Erling Haaland incident as Howard Webb takes action
Sports.content:
Man Utd VAR stood down after Erling Haaland incident as Howard Webb takes action

The video assistant referees at the centre of the Erling Haaland Manchester United vs Man City controversy in the Premier League have been stood down by Pro Ref

View 2 Images Erling Haaland's goal against Manchester United was controversially allowed to stand after a lengthy VAR check (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus have been stood down from officiating duty in the wake of the Manchester derby controversy. Donohue and Antrobus were in the video assistant referee booth for Sunday's 1-0 win for Manchester City over rivals United after Erling Haaland's second-half winner.

‌



Chief Refereeing Officer Howard Webb and the management team are said to have made the decision, which will see the pair out of action at least until after the international break. It comes after Haaland's effort was given despite the on-field decision initially being offside.

‌



It was claimed at the time that the Norwegian was in an onside position with Patrick Dorgu's outstretched leg playing him on and Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, hadn't interfered with play despite making an attempt to connect with Josko Gvardiol's cross.

‌



Robin van Persie lands new job as ex-Man Utd ace recovers from shock managerial exit READ MORE :

OPINION Erling Haaland and Man City are now on a mission to prove a point about Pep Guardiola by Andy Dunn

Lisandro Martinez was caught between the offside Fernandez and Haaland, who was behind him. The Argentine was left incensed by the decision and was forced to hold back during an angry interview with Sky Sports on Sunday.

Michael Carrick was also left exasperated from the incident and admitted he was left 'very worried' by the perception from the officials. Pro Ref, formerly the PGMOL, later apologised for an 'error of judgement'.

‌



A Pro Ref spokesperson said: "Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday's Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland's awarded goal.

"The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland - that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

‌



"In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

View 2 Images Haaland's goal was eventually given after a long VAR check (Image: Getty Images)

"Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place."

Article continues below

Donohue was the lead video assistant referee for the Manchester derby and has not been appointed a top-flight fixture this weekend, a first this term after being involved in three Premier League matches so far. He will not be on duty for the Carabao Cup third round either which sees European clubs in cup action.

The organisation were forced to U-turn on the suggestion that the former Chelsea man hadn't interfered with play following an Premier League Match Centre tweet on X.

It read: "VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball."

Sports.title: Erling Haaland and Man City are now on a mission to prove a point about Pep Guardiola
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland and Man City are now on a mission to prove a point about Pep Guardiola

The world's best manager left at the end of last season after ten glorious and successful years but Enzo Maresca has got his Manchester City side refreshed and raring to go

View 3 Images Erling Haaland could not stop smiling after Manchester City's win at Old Trafford (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Arne Slot’s version of Liverpool in the early stages of the 2025-26 season is a warning to any Premier League manager. Five Premier League matches, five wins, including a victory in the Merseyside derby.

‌



And Slot already had a title in the bank. So when it comes to reading significance into a small sample of games in August and September, the reservations are obvious.

‌



But watching Manchester City on and off the pitch at Old Trafford, it was hard not to wonder if this is a squad that has been re-energised by the managerial change. That sounds heinous to suggest, obviously.

‌



And don’t forget, Pep Guardiola did bow out by winning two trophies in his final season and his team finished as Premier League runners-up. Hardly a shabby campaign.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



But even though Guardiola also counted a Manchester derby win - a less controversial 3-0 verdict at the Etihad - amongst his early successes last season, his side lost two of their opening four Premier League games. Enzo Maresca has won four out of four, complementing those wins with a 2-0 Champions League victory in Porto.

All four Premier League wins have been in different styles but the players have quickly bought into Maresca, it seems. Not just the players.

Everyone is happy if your club has just won a Manchester derby with ten men on opposition turf. That goes without saying.

‌



View 3 Images Enzo Maresca has had the perfect start as Manchester City manager (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

But the reaction of the backroom staff - of which there were plenty - was as involved and as euphoric as City supporters have probably seen for quite some time. Again, it is understandable when you win by a single goal at Old Trafford, having had a player very harshly dismissed early doors.

But it was still significant. If some players and staff have been refreshed by a change of voice and approach, it would not be the biggest surprise. Guardiola was a very demanding manager. Brilliant but demanding, a perfectionist.

‌



Maresca could well turn out to be similarly demanding, but he is still getting to know the different characters at the club. The jury will be out for some time on Maresca’s chances of making a decent fist of the impossible job of following a decade of Pep’s brilliance. Of course it will. He will be measured in trophies.

But derby wins for City do not come much more treasured than the one he helped produce at Old Trafford. Tactically, he got it spot-on, his deployment of Iliman Ndiaye a mini masterstroke. And it is clear he likes a gritty player. Who doesn’t?

View 3 Images Pep Guardiola delivered hundreds of half-time speeches to his Manchester City players (Image: Prime Video)

‌



Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez were arch-disruptors against United and you can expect Maresca’s City to be perhaps a little more feisty than they were under Guardiola. And you can expect them to rise to the challenge.

Guardiola is and was a genius. But Erling Haaland and the players he has left at the Etihad - and, true, a few have gone - will be out to prove a point.

It might only be subconsciously, but they will be out to prove that City’s success over the past ten years was not just down to one man. And perhaps that is why the celebrations at the end of the derby win were even more euphoric.
