World.title: People's different heat perception complicating energy poverty calculations
World.content:
Although Estonia's energy poverty situation looks relatively good on paper, individual indicators may not provide the full picture, according to a University of Tartu researcher.

Energy poverty generally refers to a situation in which a person is unable to maintain a comfortable temperature in their home. However, energy poverty is not separately defined in Estonian law and comparing countries is also difficult because people's perceptions of what is warm enough vary.

"We don't have a Europe-wide measure that says if it's 21 degrees Celsius in a room in your home, that means it's warm enough. We don't have a single temperature that tells us we're warm," said Hanna Laius, a project manager at the University of Tartu's Johan Skytte Institute of Political Studies. For example, in one country a room temperature of 21 degrees Celsius may be considered perfectly adequate, while in another, 25 degrees may be considered comfortable. People's own assessments therefore also affect how energy poverty appears in statistics.

Laius said that pensioners, single parents and people living in rural areas are among the more vulnerable groups in Estonia. In addition to income, the condition of a person's home is also very important. Many buildings constructed during the Soviet era are poorly insulated and require more energy to heat.

"If, so to speak, the wind is blowing in through the gaps around your windows, you can turn the heat up as much as it will go, but you simply won't be able to get your home warm enough if it doesn't retain heat at all," Laius added.

The University of Tartu's Energy Poverty Nexus project is now working to establish an energy poverty observatory in Estonia. In addition to government agencies, the plan is to involve universities, energy companies and the Estonian Union of Co-operative Housing Associations in its work.

One of the observatory's key tasks would be to monitor energy poverty indicators and statistics and make them more comparable with those of other European countries. "Monitoring is very good in some countries, while in others it is still, so to speak, in its infancy. [Work needs to be done] to ensure that the indicators are also comparable across Europe," Laius said.

The observatory should help assess which subsidies and other measures actually reduce energy poverty. According to Laius, improving the energy efficiency of homes would provide a more lasting solution than temporarily compensating people for their energy bills. In other words, the less heat a home loses, the less fluctuations in energy prices affect a household's ability to make ends meet.

World.title: Gallery: Estonian teachers, rescuers protest for higher public sector pay
World.content:
Teachers and rescuers gathered outside the Riigikogu in Tallinn on Monday to demand higher public sector wages in the government's 2027 state budget.

Estonian Education Personnel Union (EHL) chair Reemo Voltri said the country's governing parties — the Reform Party and Eesti 200 — promised to bring teachers' pay to a competitive level by 2027.

In reality, he noted, teachers' minimum monthly salary has instead fallen six percentage points relative to the national average wage in recent years.

A fresh union survey found that two-thirds of teachers have considered leaving the profession over the past year.

"This should be a very serious warning sign for the government," Voltri said.

He noted that a strong country needs not only strong defense capabilities but also a strong education system, "and teachers who can help shape our youth into an educated generation of critical thinkers."

Kalle Koop, chief representative of the Estonian Rescue Workers' Union (EPTAÜ) and a co-organizer of the protest, also stressed the importance of internal security.

"If we don't value the work of rescuers, police officers and emergency dispatchers with competitive pay today, it'll be too late tomorrow to discover that the front line is understaffed when a crisis hits," Koop warned.

World.title: Iraq, France sign agreements to enhance economic, defense capacities
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and French President Emmanuel Macron sponsored on Monday a ceremony to sign six different memoranda of understanding at the Élysée Palace in Paris.

These agreements aim to boost Iraq’s economic, defense, and infrastructural capacities through strategic partnerships with France.

The accords overseen by the two leaders include air defense, military supply, energy supplies, civil aviation, development finance, and youth and innovation support.

Both countries reached two significant security agreements. The first is a letter of intent signed by the Iraqi Ministry of Defense and Harmattan AI for strategic air defense collaboration.

The second is a declaration of intent with the French Ministry of the Armed Forces to procure military equipment to assist Iraq in rebuilding its defensive capabilities.

The Iraqi Ministry of Electricity and French energy giant TotalEnergies inked an important cooperation document involving a gas supply and sale deal. The agreement expands existing regional initiatives to recover associated gas for power plants.

The transportation ministries of both countries signed a declaration of intent to work directly on improving civil aviation operations.

The French and Iraqi foreign ministries signed a declaration of intent to deepen Iraq’s collaboration with the French Development Agency (AFD).

The final agreement establishes an official collaboration structure between the French and Iraqi foreign ministries to promote research, innovation, and professional prospects for young people.

World.title: Iraq reviews work with foreign banks, credit rating with Rothschild & Co.
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Edouard de Rothschild of Rothschild & Co. discussed on Monday cooperation with international banks and strategies to improve Iraq’s credit rating.

During their meeting in the French capital, Paris, the two sides discussed approaches to expand Iraq’s cooperation with foreign banks, as well as the Iraqi government’s efforts to develop the banking sector, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The discussions also focused on the Iraqi government’s objectives in building a strong and diversified economy.

Rothschild highlighted Iraq’s investment potential and the approaches in which foreign financial institutions might contribute to the country’s development objectives.

The prime minister’s meeting with Rothschild is part of his diplomatic agenda in Paris. Al-Zaidi also met with French President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace to discuss regional security and energy supply channels.

Al-Zaidi held a separate meeting with TotalEnergies CEO Patrick Pouyanne to discuss a multibillion-dollar expansion of Iraq’s oil and gas production capability.

Following his trip to France, the Iraqi prime minister is planned to fly to the German capital, Berlin, to continue his European tour.

World.title: Three talking points from the Spanish Grand Prix
World.content:
Madrid – Eight wins, the most by an Italian driver in a single season, and blessed with good fortune as well as extreme talent, it is no longer a question of if Kimi Antonelli will win the drivers’ world championship, but when?

In a season of uncertain length, with the final two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi remaining in doubt, there are various permutations in terms of the points likely to be required for an unassailable advantage.

As Antonelli closes in on becoming Italy’s first champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, AFP Sport looks at three talking points from Sunday’s processional Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring circuit:

More records ready to be broken by Antonelli

The 20-year-old prodigy from Bologna already has a lead of 81 points ahead of his Mercedes team-mate George Russell, who has abandoned talking of his own title bid.

If the season includes a two-race finale in the Middle East, where the US-Israeli war with Iran makes this doubtful, he will need 153 points, from the 233 available, to become champion.

A total of 152 might be enough, thanks to his tie-breaking supremacy in number of race wins -– offering up the prospect of Antonelli taking his maiden title in Singapore next month.

But if the season is reduced from 23 races to 22 with a final race taking place at Imola, close to Antonelli’s home town, on December 6, a reduced maximum of 208 points will be on offer and the target falls to 127 –- which may be achievable in Mexico on November 1.

If he succeeded in Mexico, he would take the title aged 20 years, two months and eight days — thus reducing the record for youngest world champion held by four-time champion Sebastian Vettel by three years.

Norris’s bad luck with safety rules

World champion Lando Norris described himself as “insanely unlucky” not to win Sunday’s race as a result of the timing of a Virtual Safety Car (VSC) that was called seconds after he passed the pit lane entry.

It cost him a “cheap” pit stop and handed the initiative to his rivals, Charles Leclerc of Ferrari and Antonelli, who waited for the Monegasque driver to make his essential pit-stop before seizing victory with aplomb.

Antonelli and others pitted during the VSC, saving time and gaining an approximate 20-seconds advantage on Norris who had to fight back from fifth to finish third behind four-time champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull.

It was clearly unfair on Norris to be penalised for being the fastest driver on track and leading at the time when Lance Stroll lost control of his Aston Martin and went into the barriers.

“It is a rule that should not define a whole race,” said Norris. “I was the only one on the whole grid that didn’t get the chance to do the pit stop.”

His McLaren team boss Andrea Stella said: “Perhaps there’s a wider reflection that the F1 community should apply, as to whether you keep things like they are — or you introduce ways of maintaining more fairness.”

Honda make changes

Fernando Alonso was more than two seconds off the pace when he was eliminated from qualifying at his home race on Saturday, a clear sign his Honda-powered Aston Martin was lacking power.

As the two-time world champion publicly ponders his future, Honda announced a change of leadership for their engine programme. It may, however, be too late to persuade Alonso to stay for another year.

World.title: Germany seeks guarantees from Italy’s UniCredit over Commerzbank takeover
World.content:
Frankfurt – Germany’s finance minister was due on Monday to meet the UniCredit CEO to seek guarantees over the future of Commerzbank, as the Italian lender gears up to complete a takeover of its German rival.

Lars Klingbeil would urge UniCredit boss Andrea Orcel to protect jobs in Germany and ensure Commerzbank remains a key lender to the country’s small- and medium-sized businesses, Berlin said.

Despite fierce resistance from Berlin and the German lender, UniCredit has built up a stake of nearly 50 percent in Commerzbank and is close to sealing one of Europe’s biggest banking mergers in recent years.

A German finance ministry spokesman conceded the banks had moved into a “a different phase now” and were negotiating a transaction.

But he stressed Klingbeil wanted to ensure Commerzbank’s interests and the country’s were protected during the talks in Berlin.

“Commerzbank has over 40,000 employees and we naturally want to safeguard their interests,” he told a press conference.

Commerzbank’s “core business model” in financing Germany’s small businesses, which form the backbone of Europe’s biggest economy, should be preserved too, he said.

It was also key that Commerzbank’s main operations remained in Frankfurt to ensure the city continued as “one of the most important financial centres in Europe,” the spokesman said.

– Banking behemoth –

Berlin still believes it has some influence over the deal through its representation on Commerzbank’s supervisory board and its roughly 12-percent stake in the bank, both legacies of a state bailout during the financial crisis.

But its leverage is now likely to be diminished given the size of UniCredit’s stake.

UniCredit started building up its holding in Commerzbank in 2024 in a bid to launch a takeover.

Commerzbank slashed thousands of jobs and hiked its financial targets in an effort to convince shareholders to back its campaign to remain independent.

But these efforts failed and, with UniCredit closing in on a controlling stake, Commerzbank’s CEO Bettina Orlopp called in late July for “constructive” talks with the Italian lender.

UniCredit wants to create a European banking behemoth better able to take on bigger US rivals and argues that a merger would strengthen the region’s fragmented banking sector.

Despite resistance in Germany, some policymakers in Brussels and at the European Central Bank have been more supportive of a possible takeover.

World.title: Saudi football body vows action against Jota chants, Ronaldo urges life ban
World.content:
Riyadh – Saudi Arabian football authorities promised to take action and Cristiano Ronaldo called for life bans after rival fans taunted Al-Hilal’s Ruben Neves about the death of Diogo Jota, his friend and former Portugal team-mate.

Chants about Jota, the Liverpool and Portugal forward who died in a car crash last year, rang out during Al-Hilal’s 6-0 away win over Al-Taawoun on Saturday.

“The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour,” Saudi-based Portugal captain Ronaldo wrote on Instagram on Sunday.

“People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again,” he added.

Midfielder Neves, 29, reacted to the chants coming from the stands by sarcastically giving a thumbs-up and applauding, before pointing towards the sky.

“I just hope they don’t go to pray later after what they did,” he said after the match.

Neves was one of Jota’s closest friends and was a pallbearer at his funeral. Jota, 28, and his brother Andre, 25, died in a crash in Spain in July 2025.

The Saudi Arabian Football Federation and Saudi Pro League condemned “unacceptable conduct by some supporters” in a joint statement late on Sunday.

“Exploiting personal tragedies for the purpose of abuse or provocation is unacceptable behaviour that has no place in Saudi football,” the statement said.

“Relevant committees have identified the conduct in question and will take the necessary action in accordance with the applicable regulations and procedures,” it added.

Saudi Arabia will host the 2034 World Cup, one of the flagship events underpinning its drive to diversify an economy still heavily dependent on oil.

The powerful Gulf monarchy has invested nearly two billion dollars in football over three years, attracting stars such as Ronaldo, Neymar and Karim Benzema.

World.title: IFC appoints Thomas Jacobs to lead Iraq and regional private sector investment
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The International Finance Corporation has selected Thomas Jacobs as its new Division Director for Iraq, the Levant, and Yemen, overseeing the World Bank Group’s private-sector development efforts in the area.

Jacobs will take over IFC efforts in Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, the West Bank, and Gaza, following Khawaja Aftab Ahmed after four years in the role.

Based in Amman, Jacobs will collaborate with governments, companies, and development partners to increase private capital and employment growth.

His top priority will be infrastructure investment, access to credit for small and medium-sized enterprises, digitalization, and water security, as well as establishing conditions for increased private-sector engagement.

These sectors are especially important for Iraq as it strives to attract more international investment, diversify its oil-dependent economy, and give private enterprises a bigger role in infrastructure and jobs.

Jacobs joined the World Bank Group in 2003 and has held several senior roles in the Middle East and Asia.

He previously worked in Cairo and Beirut and most recently served as temporary division director for East Asia and the Pacific after a stint as country manager in Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia.

IFC is the World Bank Group’s private-sector arm, offering investment and consultancy services targeted at mobilizing private resources in emerging countries.

World.title: TotalEnergies to raise investments in Iraq to $16 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chairman and CEO of TotalEnergies, Patrick Pouyanne, stated on Monday that the company’s investments in Iraq’s oil and gas sectors are currently valued at $12 billion, with intentions to increase this amount to $16 billion in the future.

Pouyanne’s remarks took place during his meeting with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi in Paris, where they reviewed the company’s strategic projects in Iraq, particularly in the gas sector, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi detailed the government’s strategies to improve the recovery of associated gas and achieve self-sufficiency. He also discussed plans to boost oil production over the next five years, aiming for Iraq to reach a production target of 10 million barrels per day.

The prime minister noted that efforts are underway to broaden the scope of oil exploration in Iraq to benefit the national economy and support development objectives.

Al-Zaidi also mentioned that preparations are ongoing to organize an international energy conference in Baghdad.

Pouyanne underlined TotalEnergies’ readiness to collaborate with Iraq in the energy industries.

The French company’s commitment to its projects in Iraq highlights the significance of the Iraqi market within the framework of the European energy strategy.

This significance is especially relevant as major corporations navigate the risks posed by regional tensions while investing in one of the richest oil producers in the region.

World.title: Nigerian oil refinery Dangote launches IPO
World.content:
Lagos – Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote on Monday launched what is slated as Africa’s biggest initial public offering (IPO), which aims to raise $1.6 billion to expand his mega oil refinery to become the world’s largest.

The Lagos-based refinery, which began operations in 2024, has a capacity of 700,000 barrels per day, exceeding domestic demand in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.

It began exporting its fuel abroad a few months ago.

The Dangote Petroleum Refinery aims to raise funds to double its capacity to 1.4 million barrels a day by 2028, which would make it the world’s largest refinery, surpassing Jamnagar in India.

Describing it as an “historic day”, Dangote said in a statement that the IPO was “not simply about listing a company. It is about listing a new possibility for Nigeria, and for Africa”.

Investors can buy as few as 10 shares at 525 naira each, potentially raising 2.15 trillion naira ($1.6 billion) in a move Dangote hopes will give ordinary people a chance for a stake in a long-term asset.

He has said the offering, which closes October 13, will be the biggest IPO in African history and has encouraged participation by small investors, including people on lower incomes.

Dangote also plans to build a 700,000 barrel-per-day east African oil refinery in Lamu, on the Kenyan coast.

World.title: Jethmalani: Why wasn't FIR slapped on Varma?
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Leading lawyers Harish Salve and Mahesh Jethmalani Monday advocated a reset in the judiciary, as happened after the Emergency, and said the complaint redressal mechanism needs to be reformed for the public to continue reposing faith in the institution.

Referring to the unprecedented discovery of burning cash at Justice Yashwant Varma's residence in March last year, Jethmalani asked why an FIR was not registered given that the judge had repeatedly moved the SC seeking the quashing of the inquiry.

Jethmalani said there is a dire need for the infusion of transparency in the working of the judiciary. Salve asked if a minister would have escaped an FIR if such an incident had happened at their residence.

What would have been the judiciary's response to a PIL on such an incident being reported from the residence of a person who was not part of the judiciary.

CJI Surya Kant, responding to the queries at the Ram Jethmalani Memorial Lecture, said the internal mechanism to deal with complaints against judges is robust, responsive, and expeditious.

"No doubt every system and mechanism can be improved. But I can assure you that the internal mechanism to deal with complaints against judges has been adequate," he said.





CJI Kant said most of the complaints against judges are filed by disgruntled litigants after suffering a reversal in court.

"Would it be proper to adjudicate these complaints in the public domain? If so done, what happens to the judges and the judiciary?" the chief justice asked.

Salve said the courts must stick to their field: the law.

"When they deviate from that, the results have been devastating. Court-monitored investigations are a myth.

What happened in the 2G spectrum allocation scam, coal block allocation scam, and Hawala scam cases, investigations into which were monitored by courts? When the court monitors an investigation, the investigating agency loses its independence and feels obliged to deliver results, and that is when things get skewed," Salve said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He said a strong judiciary is welcome. "When it is strong at a time when govt is weak, everyone applauds it for raising questions.

But when there is a strong govt, the public judges the judiciary on how often it raises questions before the govt. It is then that the balance between the three organs gets disturbed," he said.

Jethmalani criticised the opaqueness in the appointments and transfers of judges in constitutional courts and said the area needs reforms to allay apprehensions of favouritism and nepotism.

CJI Kant said the collegium system has evolved over the years, and the smooth manner in which the appointments and transfers take place in consultations with govt shows that there is little reason to doubt its efficacy.

World.title: Indian travel vlogger claims ‘arrest’ by Afghan ‘Mujahideen’, seeks help
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A popular Indian travel vlogger from Kerala, who has been travelling in Afghanistan and posting videos from the country, on Monday claimed that she had been "arrested" by the "Mujahideen" in Bamyan and appealed for help in contacting the Indian embassy.

In a post on her Facebook page, the vlogger, "Backpacker Arunima", shared what she described as a translation of an official communication from local authorities, stating that she had been arrested by the Mujahideen in Afghanistan.

"You were arrested by Mujahideen just now because you do not have an official letter," the translated message read.

World.title: 'Triumph of truth over jhooth ki goonj': PM Modi hails BJP victory in Rajasthan civic polls
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Monday thanked the people of Rajasthan after the BJP emerged as the largest party in the stateâs municipal elections, winning more wards than the Congress and securing majorities in four of the 10 municipal corporations.

In a post on X, PM Modi said the results reflected support for the BJPâs policies of development and good governance under the âdouble-engine governmentâ.

âHeartfelt thanks to the people of Rajasthan for delivering a resounding victory to the BJP in the municipal elections,â PM Modi wrote.

âThis is a testament to the triumph of truth over the jhooth ki goonj (echo of lies),â he added.

PM Modi also congratulated the winning candidates and BJP workers, saying the mandate would strengthen the partyâs resolve to work towards development and prosperity in the state.

BJP ahead of Congress in urban polls

According to figures from the Rajasthan State Election Commission, results for 10,235 of the stateâs 10,244 wards had been declared by 8.30 pm on Monday.

The BJP had won 4,179 wards compared with 3,613 for the Congress. The BJP crossed the majority mark in Jaipur, Udaipur, Kota and Bhilwara municipal corporations, while the Congress secured a majority in Bikaner.

The Congress also recorded a major victory in the Jhalawar municipal council, considered a stronghold of former chief minister Vasundhara Raje.





The elections covered 309 urban local bodies â 10 municipal corporations, 47 municipal councils and 252 municipal boards.

BJP crosses majority in Kota

In Kota Municipal Corporation, the BJP secured 55 of the 100 wards, while Congress won 40 and Independents three. The result for Ward 87 was put on hold after an EVM malfunction.

Congress candidate Laxmi Sharma and other party workers staged a protest outside the counting centre, seeking the result and alleging irregularities.

Officials later sealed the machine in the presence of the district collector and additional district magistrate and forwarded a report to the Election Commission through the returning officer.

The BJP also retained several individual seats. Vivek Rajvanshi won his fourth consecutive term from Ward 54, defeating Congress candidate Manish by 2,226 votes.

Gopal Ram Manda secured his fifth consecutive election victory, defeating Congress candidate Sanjay Yadav by 899 votes.

Congress and Independent candidates, however, registered victories in some key wards. Youth Congress candidate Arpit Jain defeated BJP veteran and former deputy mayor Yogendra Khinchi by 250 votes in Ward 86.

Independent candidate Vandana Faujdar won Ward 71 with 1,264 votes, defeating BJP candidate Meenakshi Sen by 160 votes.

Independents give BJP majority in Bundi

In Bundi, the BJP initially emerged as the largest party with 29 wards, two short of a majority.

Congress won 20 wards, while Independents secured 11.

Later in the day, three Independent candidates, Prabhat Devi, Aatmaram Chopdar and Vishal Sharma, joined the BJP, taking the party to a majority and enabling it to form the board.

The BJP had also captured the previous mid-term board after Congress council chairperson Madu Nuwal was suspended.

Congress leaders had expected to retain control but faced criticism over ticket distribution.

Former councillors Devraj Gochar, Ankit Buliwal and Jeeshan Ali, who were denied Congress tickets, won as Independents.

BJP calls results a mandate for governance

BJP president Nitin Nabin thanked Rajasthan voters for what he described as a âhistoric victoryâ, saying the results showed continued faith in Modiâs leadership.

World.title: Yogi Adityanath announces welfare measures, tech push for lawyers in UP
World.content:
PRAYAGRAJ: Chief minister

on Monday took a swipe at the previous Samajwadi Party government, saying that before 2017, the state faced not only a shortage of resources but also issues related to governance, transparency, accountability, law and order, and judicial infrastructure.

Additionally, the chief minister revealed plans to provide tablets to 400 state law officers to equip them with modern technology, enabling them to access information on government-related cases before the courts.

In another announcement, Adityanath said the state government would introduce a cashless insurance scheme providing coverage of up to Rs 5 lakh for practising advocates in

.

Addressing a felicitation ceremony organised by the Allahabad High Court Bar Association here, Adityanath said nearly 45 to 50 per cent posts in the Uttar Pradesh Police were vacant before his government assumed office in 2017.

"Before 2017, the challenge before us was not merely of resources. It was also a challenge of the system and approach, transparency and accountability in administration, law and order and judicial infrastructure," the chief minister said.

He highlighted that the police force's annual training capacity at that time was only about 3,000 personnel but has now increased to 60,000.

"There was no training capacity and even basic facilities for the police were lacking," Adityanath said, adding that his government has strengthened police infrastructure and training facilities across the state.





Adityanath also addressed the condition of the subordinate judiciary before 2017, pointing out that many courts operated in dilapidated or temporary buildings, and that district courts in as many as ten districts functioned from rented premises.

Furthermore, he stated that his government had also addressed several shortcomings that earlier hampered the criminal justice system, including witnesses turning hostile out of fear in serious criminal cases and inadequate arrangements for transporting prisoners from jails to courts.

"Today, you can see the results of better coordination between the executive and the judiciary. When we reform and transform, the performance becomes visible on its own," the chief minister said.

He emphasised that a robust judiciary strengthens the foundations of good governance, which should be the top priority of any elected government.

Adityanath noted hat his government has prioritised greater use of technology, modernised infrastructure, and improved coordination between police and prosecution, leading to significant increases in conviction rates.

He pointed out that the prosecution system is now connected to online platforms to ensure timely charge sheet filings and effective presentations of scientific evidence in court.

Referring to emerging challenges, Adityanath said the legal fraternity must prepare itself for areas ranging from cybercrime and artificial intelligence to data privacy, e-commerce, fintech, intellectual property and climate litigation.

"A future-ready Bar will lay a strong foundation for a future-ready justice system," he said, adding that the younger generation of lawyers has a major responsibility in carrying forward the rich traditions of the Allahabad High Court.

The chief minister said that district courts and jails have been provided with high-speed internet and video conferencing facilities. Additionally, the virtual recording of evidence and the digitization of court documents are being promoted to reduce trial delays.

"Justice delayed is justice denied," he said, stressing that timely and impartial justice was essential to maintaining public faith in the judiciary and other democratic institutions.

Integrated court complexes were being developed to provide judicial facilities, residential accommodation for judicial officers, chambers for lawyers and other amenities under one roof, he said.

Moreover, he outlined welfare measures for advocates, announcing that financial assistance from the lawyers' welfare fund has increased from Rs 1.5 lakh to Rs 5 lakh.

The age limit for financial assistance to the families of deceased advocates has also been raised from 60 to 70 years.

Adityanath said a strong judiciary forms the foundation of good governance and called for continued coordination and mutual respect between the Bar and the Bench.

"Only a future-ready Bar can lay a strong foundation for a future-ready justice system," he said.

World.title: 3 Italian passengers fly out of Delhi without immigration clearance: What exactly happened
World.content:
3 Italian passengers flew from Amritsar to Munich without immigration clearance

What exactly happened?

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The civil aviation ministry has issued a show-cause notice to Air India over alleged procedural lapses that allowed three Italian passengers to board a connecting flight from Delhi without completing immigration formalities earlier this month.The notice has been issued to the Air India CEO.The home ministry has also convened a meeting of stakeholders on Tuesday to discuss the incident, sources told news agency PTI.The three passengers flew from Amritsar to Delhi on September 4 before boarding a Lufthansa flight to Munich from Delhi airport. However, they did not complete the required immigration formalities at the airport, sources added.Titled âviolation of SOP for hub and spoke operations resulting in three foreign nationals departing India without mandatory immigration clearance,â the show-cause notice issued to Air India last Saturday said the three passengers arrived in Delhi from Amritsar on AI 1115 at 12.50 am on September 4 and subsequently departed for Munich on a codeshare Lufthansa flight at 1.45 am, within an hour of their arrival.Home secretary Govind Mohan will chair a meeting on Tuesday to discuss the incident.The secretary and additional secretary of the civil aviation ministry, Intelligence Bureau director, additional secretary (UT and Foreigners) of the home ministry, Bureau of Immigration commissioner, Air India CEO and Delhi airport CEO are expected to attend the meeting, they added.Amritsar airport is among the airports where Air India operates flights under its âHub-and-Spokeâ model.Under this arrangement, passengers complete immigration formalities at the airport of origin and can then travel to an overseas destination through a designated hub. At the hub airport, where the international flight departs, passengers are required only to undergo security checks before boarding.For a passenger travelling from Amritsar via Delhi to an international destination, Amritsar serves as the spoke and Delhi as the hub.In the case of the three Italian passengers, sources said they were issued boarding passes at Amritsar for both their flight to Delhi and the Lufthansa flight to Munich.However, as the two flights were not covered under Air Indiaâs âHub-and-Spokeâ model, the passengers were required to exit through the arrival area at Delhi and complete immigration formalities before taking the Lufthansa flight.After arriving at Delhi airport, they were instead taken to the international transfer area and did not reach the immigration counter. They then boarded the flight to Munich without completing the immigration process, the sources said, as cited by PTI.Air India and Lufthansa have an interline partnership. An interline agreement generally allows passengers to book connecting flights operated by different airlines under a single itinerary.

Nearly 50 lakh people across 15 districts of Bihar have been affected by floods as heavy rain in recent days caused rivers already flowing above danger levels to swell further, officials said on Monday.Bihar has recorded 112.7 mm of rainfall so far this month, about six per cent above normal, according to the local weather office.According to the Disaster Management Department, floods have affected 49.67 lakh people across 15 districts in Bihar.The affected districts include Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnea, Madhepura and Araria.An official said incessant rain in the catchment areas of rivers flowing from Nepal into Bihar, along with heavy rainfall in the state, has pushed several rivers and streams above their danger marks, as cited by PTI.The Ganga was flowing at 36.19 metres at Sultanganj in Bhagalpur at 6.00 pm on Monday, 1.69 metres above the danger level.The Kosi river was flowing above the danger mark at Baltara and Kursela, while the Budhi Gandak had crossed the danger level at Khagaria.The Ganga was above the danger mark at Digha, Gandhi Ghat, Hathidah, Bhagalpur, Kahalgaon and Munger. The Punpun at Sripalpur, Bagmati at Benibad and Ghaghara at Darauli were also flowing above their respective danger levels.The administration has set up 1,248 community kitchens and 13 relief camps in the flood-hit areas. Around 11,508 people have been provided accommodation, food, medical care and other essential facilities, officials said.The Disaster Management Department said the Gandak barrage at Valmiki Nagar recorded a water discharge of 1,09,000 cusecs at 4 pm on Monday, with the flow continuing to rise.At the Kosi Barrage in Birpur, the discharge stood at 1,63,315 cusecs, against this year's highest flow of 2,55,425 cusecs recorded on July 20.Twenty-seven teams of the State Disaster Response Force and 10 teams of the National Disaster Response Force have been deployed across various districts for relief and rescue operations.

World.title: Intensify protest over land acquisition: Rakesh Tikait urges Noida farmers
World.content:
Bharatiya Kisan Union leader Rakesh Tikait on Monday (September 14, 2026) asked farmers and villagers protesting over their pending demands in Gautam Buddh Nagar to continue their agitation, saying "struggle is the only option" left before them.

Addressing protesting farmers at the offices of the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA), Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority (GNIDA) and Noida Authority, Mr. Tikait assured them of his organisation's support and urged them to remain at the protest sites.

"If you cannot enter the office of your local authority, meet officials or raise your issues, are you a hostage or a prisoner? If farmers cannot meet their own officials, struggle is the only option left before them," Mr. Tikait said.

The farmers have been seeking developed residential plots and enhanced compensation for land acquired for development projects. Their demands include 10% developed 'abadi' plots in lieu of acquired land and an additional 64% compensation, besides greater flexibility in using residential plots and more 'abadi' land in villages.

The Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU) national spokesperson alleged that the administration was preventing farmers from holding protests and meeting officials, leaving them with no alternative but to continue their agitation.

"Whatever they do now, they will have to struggle. I will stand with these people. My support is with them. I tell you to stay here and continue your protest," he said.

Mr. Tikait, a prominent face of the anti-farm laws agitation in 2020-21, said that earlier farmer protests could often be resolved through dialogue as the government also responded positively to such efforts. "But that situation no longer exists. Now people will have to struggle. The time has come when people have to take the path of struggle," he said.

Mr. Tikait met groups of protesting farmers at the three authority offices, sat with them on the protest stage and assured them of the BKU's support.

BKU national general secretary Pawan Khatan earlier said farmers had held meetings and conducted village-to-village outreach ahead of the September 14 Kisan Mahapanchayat under Tikait's leadership.

World.title: Houthis say Saudi Arabia hits Yemen with 54 strikes after attack on bases
World.content:
Yemen's Houthis said on Monday (September 14, 2026) that Saudi Arabia launched airstrikes across the west of the country after the Iran-backed group earlier announced it targeted military bases in the kingdom.

The group, fighting the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government, last week seized control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which has become vital as the wider U.S.-Iran war chokes the Strait of Hormuz.

The Houthis said Riyadh targeted Yemen with 54 strikes over 24 hours, after the group fired dozens of drones and missiles at Saudi military facilities, prompting the Saudi civil defence to issue alerts in the southern cities of Khamis Mushait and Abha.

The civil defence later issued a brief alert for Najran in southwestern Saudi Arabia without elaborating on the cause for the warning.

A Khamis Mushait resident said he heard "intense blasts" which left fires burning for a "long time". "Honestly, we couldn't sleep at all."

Houthi missile attacks in western Yemen killed eight troops from Yemeni government forces, two military sources with the Aden-based administration told AFP.

The Iran-backed group's Al-Masirah TV channel said two civilians were killed in Saudi strikes that destroyed a bridge in Taiz province, which has seen some of Yemen's fiercest clashes in recent days.

The renewed fighting in Yemen comes as the wider regional war remains at a stalemate. But U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday said he was open to holding talks with Iran.

"The failing Nation of Iran wants to make a deal, quickly and badly. I will determine whether or not the U.S.A. will choose to engage — The concept of which we are open to," Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network.

World.title: Govt. bars bank charges on payments up to ₹2,000 via UPI, RuPay-powered debit cards

India on ​Monday (September 14, 2026) notified changes ‌in the Payment And ​Settlement ⁠Act, 2007, specifying that banks cannot impose charges ‌on payments via ‌Unified Payments ‌Interface (UPI) transactions ⁠of up ⁠to ₹2,000.

A government gazette ​notification ‌specified RuPay-powered debit cards and UPI transactions of ‌up to ​₹2,000 as electronic ⁠modes of payment.

It said ‌no bank or system provider shall impose any direct or indirect ‌charge on ​a person making or receiving payments ⁠through these modes.

The notification altered ⁠an earlier provision that prevented banks from charging fees on digital payments via India’s popular UPI, paving the ‌way for charges to be imposed on larger transfers.

A final decision on ‌whether to introduce charges, and ‌how they ⁠would be levied, has yet to ⁠be taken.

World.title: Pakistan court orders blocking passports of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa CM, 24 lawmakers of Imran Khan's party
World.content:
An Islamabad anti-terrorism court on Monday (September 14, 2026) ordered the blocking of passports of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Muhammad Sohail Afridi and 24 other Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) lawmakers in connection with a case registered at a police station in the national capital.

Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain issued the order while allowing a request by the police and directed the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to block the passports until further orders.

The order also covers senior PTI leader and former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser, lawmakers Shahram Khan Tarakai, Shah Ahmad, Sher Ali Arbab, Muhammad Iqbal Afridi, Dr Amjad Ali, Junaid Akbar, Shahid Khattak, Zubair Wazir, Arshad Umarzai, Zar Alam, Mian Omar and Akhtar Khan, among others.

The court said the available record showed that the individuals have been named as accused in the case.

The investigating officer told the court that the accused could flee the country to evade legal proceedings and alleged that they were facing serious charges, including attacks on state institutions and promotion of terrorism.

The court noted that the accused had failed to appear before it and that those who had secured interim bail had also not yet joined the investigation.

It subsequently approved the police request and ordered the FIA to keep the passports blocked until further orders.

The order comes amid heightened political activity by the PTI, which has announced a nationwide protest for September 27.

Mr. Afridi, who is currently touring Punjab to mobilise support for the planned protest, separately alleged on Monday (September 14, 2026) that Punjab Police had attempted to abduct him and later left him on the roadside after assaulting and mistreating him.

"Punjab Police will have to answer for this action. This is no joke," Mr. Afridi said, describing the alleged treatment of a chief minister of one province by police of another province as "unacceptable".

He demanded an explanation from the Punjab government over why he was allegedly left on the roadside and mistreated.

The PTI has in recent months remained engaged in political agitation against the central government, with its supporters and leaders facing multiple cases linked to protests and alleged violence against state institutions.

World.title: Kerala HC issues notice to Mani C. Kappan on petition seeking disqualification as Pala MLA
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has issued notice to Pala MLA Mani C. Kappan on a petition seeking his disqualification as an elected representative.

The petition was filed by Mumbai-based businessman Dinesh Menon, who is also the complainant in the four cheque bounce cases in which Mr. Kappan was convicted on September 1.

The Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Borivali, Mumbai, sentenced Mr. Kappan to a total of three and a half years' imprisonment, a fine of more than ₹3.25 crore, and additional imprisonment upon default of payment, in the cheque bounce cases.

Mr. Menon sought directions to the Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly and to the Election Commission of India, for the former to declare the Pala Assembly seat vacant as of September 1 and the latter to initiate proceedings for a by-election for the constituency.

The matter will be considered again on September 22.

World.title: Jarange-Patil vows to take Maratha quota fight to Mumbai; 10 people, two ambulances to accompany him on Sept. 15
World.content:
Denied permission for his hunger strike in Mumbai, Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange-Patil on Monday (September 14, 2026) announced he would head to the Maharashtra capital alone on September 15 to stage a protest at Azad Maidan.

Addressing supporters at Antarwali Sarati village in Jalna district on the 16th day of his indefinite fast, Mr. Jarange-Patil accused Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis of blocking the protest out of fear, and attempting to create unrest during the Ganesh festival to blame the Maratha community for it.

Police on Sunday (September 13, 2026) denied permission to Jarange for his indefinite hunger strike in Mumbai from September 19, citing potential security concerns during the Ganeshotsav festivities which began on Monday (September 14, 2026).

The police turned down a formal request from the activist's team citing possible violations of Public Meetings, Demonstrations, and Processions Rules, as well as alleged non-compliance with venue conditions during previous protests.

"Fearing the strength of the Maratha community, the government has denied permission to go to Mumbai. As a counter to the government's decision, I will leave for Mumbai alone on September 15 at 11 am," Mr. Jarange-Patil insisted.

He appealed to the Maratha community not to converge at the capital immediately, stating only 10 people and two ambulances would accompany him along the planned route starting Tuesday morning (September 15, 2026).

"Fadnavis's people will create a disturbance during the Maratha rally and blame the Maratha community. That is why I have decided to go alone. Now, will the government deny permission for my solo march as well?" he asked.

Talking to reporters in Mumbai, Chief Minister Fadnavis urged Mr. Jarange-Patil to reconsider his plan to stage a protest in Mumbai in view of the ongoing Ganesh festival, which attracts a large number of devotees to various pandals set up by community groups.

Mr. Fadnavis insisted his government never stopped dialogue with Mr. Jarange-Patil.

"Almost all demands (made by Jarange) have been met. Some demands are in court and at different stages. But then the demands cannot be met unless one approaches the court or other constitutional fora. We have apprised him about it," the CM said.

CM Fadnavis asserted the State government cannot do anything on the quota issue that is not in accordance with existing laws and will strictly abide by the Constitution. "Protesting during the Ganesh festival (which began on Monday) that may lead to inconvenience to Ganesh bhakts (devotees) is not appropriate. So this (protest in Mumbai) should be reconsidered," the BJP leader maintained.

Mr. Jarange-Patil, whose condition has deteriorated after refusing water, saline, and medical treatment, insisted he would remain firm on his demands. He urged supporters to save their resources and remain peaceful in their villages while he handled the agitation in Mumbai.

"The road ahead is full of obstacles, but I will not retreat from the struggle for the community," the 44-year-old activist maintained.

Describing himself as a follower of Maratha warrior king Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the activist said he would fight until his last breath, adding he wanted to send a message that he "died but did not surrender".

Among Mr. Jarange-Patil's main demands is that a Government Resolution (GR) be issued allowing Marathas to claim reservation available to the Kunbi community in the Other Backward Classes (OBC) category based on old records and gazette documents.

OBC groups have opposed it, claiming their share of benefits will be affected.

At the same time, Mr. Jarange-Patil said the doors for talks with the government remained open.

"We are ready to hold discussions with the government at any open ground. But we do not want hollow assurances; we want direct implementation," he said, warning political leaders that the Maratha community would decide their fate in future polls.

On August 29 last year, Mr. Jarange-Patil had launched an indefinite hunger strike at Azad Maidan in Mumbai to reiterate his demand for Maratha reservation. The agitation led to chaos in parts of the city, and it was called off after the government accepted some of his demands.

World.title: Bob Mackie, fashion designer for the stars, dies at 87
World.content:
Hollywood designer Bob Mackie, known for making stars such ​as Cher and Elton John ‌sparkle, died on Monday (September 14, 2026) at 87, ​according to a ⁠post on his official Instagram account.

His career spanned five decades and included designing a ‌Barbie doll clothes collection.

Born in 1939 into a ‌middle-class family in Monterey ‌Park, California, ⁠he was nominated for ⁠more than 30 Emmys, winning nine. He received Academy Award nominations for costumes ​worn in the films “Lady ‌Sings the Blues,” “Funny Lady,” and “Pennies From Heaven.”

“His genius and extraordinary designs will live on forever, continuing ‌to bring beauty into this ​world,” his team said in an Instagram post. His ⁠cause of death was not stated.

Mackie was known for sequins, ‌rhinestones and glitter, but also humour.

The highlight of his 11-year run for The Carol Burnett Show was the “curtain dress” worn by Burnett in a sketch parodying ‌1939 film classic “Gone with the ​Wind.” The costume, now in the collection of the Smithsonian’s ⁠American History Museum, included a brass curtain ⁠rod balanced on Burnett’s shoulders and a bit of ‌valance worn as a hat.

World.title: Underwater survey to be done to assess long-term impact of MSC Elsa 3 sinking, Centre informs Kerala HC
World.content:
The Central government informed the Kerala High Court that a multi-beam underwater survey would be carried out to assess the long-term environmental implications, marine ecological concerns, the current state of the submerged wreck and the potential future risks of the MSC Elsa 3 shipwreck.

The Liberian-flagged vessel owned by the Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) sank off the coast of Alappuzha in May 2025, reportedly causing substantial coastal and marine damage to the shores of Keralam and Tamil Nadu.

The Additional Solicitor General of India appearing for the Centre and the Ministry of Defence informed the Division Bench of Justices V. Raja Vijayaraghavan and K.V. Jayakumar that two agencies had already been identified for the underwater survey.

He stated that all measures would be taken to carry out the survey as early as possible.

The court was considering a batch of public interest litigations seeking the removal of the hazardous wreckage and compensation for fishermen affected by the incident.

World.title: KP CM claims he was 'abducted' by authorities in Lahore; Punjab minister denies allegations
World.content:
LAHORE: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday claimed he was “abducted” by authorities in Lahore and later “thrown” by the roadside, a claim denied by Punjab Information Minister.

“We were abducted, and then, when they received pressure from somewhere, they threw me by the roadside without security and left,” Afridi claimed.

Afridi further alleged that there was a “conspiracy to abduct the chief minister of a province”, adding that he had earlier warned that “they want to divide the country”.

Speaking to Dawn, a senior KP government official accompanying Afridi said the chief minister had boarded the police van to secure the release of some detained party workers. While some workers were freed, others remained in the van, prompting Afridi to refuse to leave.

The police then drove the van a reasonable distance from the spot before removing Afridi from the vehicle, he added.

However, Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari claimed that the KP chief minister had boarded a police vehicle of his own accord.

In the video shared by Bokhari, Afridi can be seen voluntarily walking towards and boarding the police vehicle. He then refuses to dismount, while an individual can be heard asking the chief minister to “please leave the vehicle”.

Speaking on Dunya News, Bokhari said that when PTI supporters swarmed the car, the police thought they were being attacked.

“There were cameras shooting them, and there was a video from inside the dala,” Azma noted. “The driver thought the vehicle was being attacked, so he drove away, but stopped a short while later and said people got off and sat on the footpath.”

Azma claimed that none of the motorists in the area bothered to note that Afridi was sitting on the footpath.

Asked if Afridi had been arrested, the minister replied in the negative, citing a lack of police at the scene and the fact that his guards and a cameraman were present.

“This is a total drama because people did not come out from Lahore and Punjab,” she added.

When asked about Afridi’s claim that he had been released under pressure and left without any security, Azma joked: “The only pressure in that scenario is his low blood pressure.”

A post on the KP chief minister’s official X account at around 9pm said Afridi “himself got on a Punjab Police van and reached a police station”. Another post, published minutes earlier, said Afridi was present with party workers at a protest rally on Lahore’s Mall Road.

‘Insult to the mandate’

KP Minister for Information Shafi Jan, in a statement, alleged that Punjab Police had attempted to abduct the KP CM, claiming that he was separated from his security detail and forcibly moved into another vehicle.

Jan alleged that Afridi was put into a police vehicle and taken to a remote area, where he was later left without his security detail after “pressure mounted”. He accused the Punjab Chief Maryam Nawaz government of “police high-handedness” and said the treatment of the elected chief minister was unconstitutional and undemocratic.

“The attempt to abduct Chief Minister Afridi will be considered an attack on the foundations of the federation,” said Jan.

He further alleged that the incident was a “dangerous attempt” to create hatred and confrontation between the two provinces, warning that any attempt to abduct an elected chief minister would be considered an attack on the foundations of the federation. He said the KP chief minister’s “humiliation” would not be tolerated.

PTI condemned the “arrest” of Afridi in Punjab, calling it an “insult” to the mandate and dignity of the people of the province.

In a statement, the party said the incident, along with recent statements by the Punjab chief minister, risked fuelling “resentment, mistrust and division” among the provinces.

PTI said it would not engage in “provincialism, ethnicity, hatred or division”, stressing that the mandate of people across all provinces must be respected.

The party urged its supporters to respond peacefully and democratically, saying repression and political victimisation would only deepen public resentment.

PTI General Secretary Salman Akram Raja said in a post on X that Afridi’s alleged abduction was an attack on the foundations of the federation and urged the police to “come to their senses”.

Afridi’s Lahore visit

Afridi turned his Lahore visit into a full-fledged political showdown, lashing out at the Punjab government, refusing security and vowing to rid the country of “fake rulers” through a nationwide street movement on Sept 27.

The KP CM changed his detailed Punjab visit plan and travelled directly to Lahore to offer condolences to the bereaved family of senior party worker, who had succumbed to his burn injuries.

As the Punjab Police escort created hurdles for party leaders and workers trying to join him, Afridi admonished the policemen, calling them “shameless” and accusing them of pushing a man to his death while he was preparing for Eid-i-Miladun Nabi celebrations. “I do not want security from a force that killed a man preparing for Eid-i-Miladun Nabi,” he said.

Responding directly to Punjab CM Maryam, who had said she felt threatened by the other three provinces, Afridi said: “The fake chief minister says she feels threatened not by India but by the other three provinces of Pakistan. I announce today that I feel no threat from my brothers and sisters in Punjab.”

The KP chief minister and his cabinet members’ convoy faced police blockades while entering Punjab and later within Lahore, where all entry and exit points had been sealed.

As Afridi and his convoy travelled through the city, tensions also ran high between police and PTI workers on several occasions, with reports of scuffles.

Earlier, the KP chief minister and his cabinet members received a rousing welcome from party workers at several points along their route. Workers chanted slogans as Afridi addressed them at Do Moriya Pul on Circular Road.

Hundreds of party workers lined the city roads, prompting the KP CM to make several stops. He waved to the crowds and raised slogans while standing through the sunroof of his vehicle.

The rally, however, caused severe traffic congestion in the Walled City, with frequent stops forcing commuters to use adjoining streets. Railway Station Road and surrounding areas, including Aik Moria Pul, Akbari Market Road, Delhi Gate, Wasanwala Bazaar and Shah Alam Market, witnessed severe traffic jams. Traffic police made unsuccessful attempts to restore the flow.

Earlier in the day, police had set up pickets on roads across the city and closed markets around the deceased party worker’s residence, as well as along major roads including Gulberg, Ferozepur Road and The Mall.

Following the imposition of Section 144 in Punjab, police attempted to disperse crowds accompanying or welcoming Afridi’s convoy and eventually arrested more than a dozen PTI workers, including PTI Lahore president Mian Akram Usman and vice-president Naeemullah Taj.

World.title: Govt increases petrol by Rs4.42 per litre, HSD by Rs6.10 per litre amid rising global oil prices
World.content:
The government on Monday increased the price of petrol by Rs4.42 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs6.10 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs380.24 per litre while HSD will cost Rs409.42 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 15 (Tuesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a “relief scheme” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

A statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said owners of two- and three-wheelers would receive relief of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles up to 800cc would receive the same relief on a monthly quota of 30 litres.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: SBP keeps interest rate unchanged at 11.5pc
World.content:
The State Bank of Pakistan’s (SBP) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) on Monday kept the key policy rate unchanged at 11.5 per cent.

The decision comes as prolonged tensions in the Middle East drive up global oil prices and fuel inflation.

In a detailed statement, the MPC said it decided to keep the policy rate unchanged with a majority decision of seven out of ten members. MPC noted the recent escalation in the Middle East conflict, which it said led to an increase in global commodity prices and persistent supply chain disruptions.

“However, recent domestic macroeconomic data turned out broadly in line with the MPC’s expectations,” the statement said, adding that headline inflation increased by 11.1pc year-on-year in August from the previous 9.2pc in July and “core inflation was slightly lower than expectations”.

“External account pressures remained contained, supported by robust workers’ remittances and higher financial inflows.”

MPC noted that economic activity picked up “as reflected by recent high-frequency indicators”.

MPC said that the current monetary policy rate was “appropriate to guide inflation towards target range of 5-7pc over the medium term”.

“However, uncertainty regarding the outlook has increased, particularly from the worsening geopolitical environment.”

Listing key developments since its last meeting, MPC noted that Pakistan’s sovereign credit rating was upgraded to B3 by Moody’s with a stable outlook.

It also noted that the country had tapped international capital markets to “raise $3bn through Eurobonds,” leading to an increase in foreign reserves to over $21bn

“Third, inflation expectations of both businesses and consumers increased in September, while their confidence weakened,” the statement read.

It also observed an output decline of 3.5pc in June in large-scale manufacturing, which it said brought the “cumulative FY26 growth to 5pc”.

“Fifth, fiscal consolidation turned out higher than the budgetary target during FY26,” it said, further noting that Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) collection had remained “on-target” during July to August in FY27.

“While SBP transferred higher profit of Rs1.9 trillion than the budgeted amount of Rs1.4tr to the government.

“Lastly, central banks have become more cautious amidst challenging global economic conditions,” it added.

The MPC said that it was committed to “achieving price stability with close monitoring of incoming data and the ongoing situation in the Middle East”.

It also observed that adverse geopolitical events as well as weather disruptions had increased in frequency, posing risks to the macroeconomic outlook.

In this regard, the MPC stressed the need for maintaining a “prudent monetary and fiscal policy mix and further buildup of buffers to absorb supply shocks”.

Before the MPC’s announcement, bankers had anticipated a status quo, but some analysts had predicted that the central bank was in a difficult position and would lift the policy rate by 50 points.

The SBP has held the rate steady since raising it by 100 basis points in April in response to rising global energy prices and supply chain risks — its first increase in nearly three years.

Before that, the central bank had maintained the rate at 10.5pc in January and March after a surprise 50bps cut in December 2025.

The SBP has cut the key rate by a cumulative 1,050 basis points since mid-2024, from a record 22pc reached in June 2023, as inflation cooled sharply from multi-decade highs.

Additional input from Reuters

World.title: New US rules change how international students can stay in America
World.content:
WASHINGTON: A major change in the US immigration system is set to take effect on Tuesday, requiring international students to keep closer track of how long they are authorised to remain in the country.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is ending the longstanding “duration of status” system for F-1 students and replacing it with a fixed period of admission.

Under the new rule, F-1 students will generally be admitted for the length of the academic programme listed on their Form I-20, up to four years, with a 30-day period to arrive before the programme begins and 30 days to prepare for departure after the programme or authorised post-completion training ends.

Students who need additional time to complete their current programme, begin a new programme, or undertake post-completion OPT or STEM OPT will have to take additional steps. They may apply to US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) for an extension of stay, or leave the United States and seek a new period of admission from Customs and Border Protection when they return.

DHS advises students to work with their college’s designated school official before applying for an extension. Students seeking an extension must file Form I-539 with USCIS after receiving the appropriate recommendation on an updated Form I-20.

What happens to students already in America?

The change does not mean that every F-1 student currently in the United States has to file a new application on Tuesday.

Students who are in the United States in F-1 status under the existing duration of status system on September 15 may remain without applying for an extension until the applicable programme or OPT/STEM OPT end date, subject to the transition rules.

Students walk on campus at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the US on November 19, 2025. — Reuters/ File

For these students, the transition period generally runs no later than November 14, 2030.

There is an important exception involving travel. Current F-1 students who leave the United States after Sept 15 may be readmitted under the new fixed-period system, rather than continuing under duration of status system.

Students who are considering international travel should therefore speak with their designated school official before leaving the country.

New rules for students’ academic plans

The rule also imposes new restrictions on changes during an F-1 student’s academic career.

Among other changes, undergraduate students generally cannot change their educational level or major during the first year of a program without an exception for extenuating circumstances.

Graduate-level students face additional restrictions on changing educational levels, majors and transferring schools.

The rule also reduces the departure period after completion of a program or post-completion OPT/STEM OPT from the previous 60 days to 30 days for students subject to the new system.

New immigration forms

The Sept 15 change also affects USCIS paperwork. Students filing Form I-539, used to request an extension or change of nonimmigrant status, or Form I-765, used to apply for employment authorisation, should use the new editions required by USCIS beginning Tuesday.

Students should check the edition date before filing because USCIS will not provide a grace period for use of the previous editions.

For international students, the most important point is that Sept. 15 is not a blanket deadline to leave America or file a new application. It marks the beginning of a new system in which admission is tied to a specific period, and students who need additional time may have to obtain an extension or a new period of admission.

Universities urge students to check travel, immigration records

Major US universities are advising international students to pay particular attention to travel plans and their Form I-94 as the new rules take effect.

Harvard University, Yale University, Columbia University, Cornell University and Stanford University have issued guidance explaining the changes and urging students to consult their international offices before making immigration or travel decisions.

Yale says students already in the United States under the old “duration of status” system generally do not need to take immediate action on Sept 15.

But students who travel abroad and return after that date will generally receive a new I-94 with a specific “admit until” date. Yale advises students to check the I-94 after every international trip.

Harvard similarly warns that international travel after Sept 15 can affect future OPT and extension-of-stay planning. Its international office advises students to understand the consequences before making travel plans.

Columbia and Cornell have also published detailed guidance on the transition rules, while Stanford has warned that F-1 and J-1 students will no longer be admitted under the D/S notation after the rule takes effect.

The message from the universities is essentially the same: students should not assume that Sept 15 itself requires them to leave or file a new application, but they should understand their individual I-94, program end date, OPT plans and the consequences of international travel.

The Department of Homeland Security is also ending the “duration of status” system for J-1 exchange visitors and certain I-visa holders, including representatives of foreign information media. They too will generally be admitted for a fixed period rather than indefinitely for the duration of their program or assignment.

J-1 participants who need additional time will generally have to seek an extension of stay, while the rules for I representatives are tied to the length of their media assignment.

The change does not apply broadly to other major nonimmigrant categories such as H-1B, L-1, O-1 or B-1/B-2 visas, which already operate under fixed periods of admission.

World.title: Govt mulling revival of austerity measures, decision to be taken soon: Tarar
World.content:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Monday that the government was considering reviving austerity measures introduced during a previous fuel conservation drive amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East.

The austerity measures were announced on March 9 to mitigate the impact of the ongoing US-Iran war. These included a 50 per cent cut in fuel allowances for official vehicles, salary cuts for lawmakers, and a partial work-from-home policy in the public sector.

Tarar made the remarks while addressing a press briefing alongside Information Technology Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja and Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik on the government’s fuel relief scheme, which was launched on Sunday amid rising oil prices.

In response to a question, the information minister said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had directed consultations on the austerity measures, some of which, he noted, “are still in force, such as market timings”.

Tarar added that “austerity measures previously taken [..] were being reviewed to assess which of the previous measures need to be revived in the present situation”.

He added that a decision will be taken soon.

The government ended the measures on June 19, except for market timings. However, in July, it emerged that it was considering shifting back to fuel conservation and austerity measures .

The move comes amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East, which have disrupted major oil supply routes and led to a rise in fuel prices.

In addition to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz stemming from the US-Iran war, trade through Bab al-Mandab — which has become a vital route for Saudi oil exports in recent months — is also facing a growing threat from Houthi rebels.

At present, the price of petrol stands at Rs375.82 per litre, while high-speed diesel (HSD) costs Rs403.32 per litre.

Relief scheme to cost around Rs25bn monthly

Speaking about the relief scheme, under which users of motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingqis and vehicles up to 800cc will receive relief of Rs100 per litre, Tarar said the premier had directed Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar to ensure that transport fares did not rise following the launch of the scheme.

Tarar also said the steering committee for the scheme would include the chief secretaries of all four provinces, Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) and Gilgit-Baltistan.

In his address, Tarar said a war room and a call centre had been established under the scheme and that “constant monitoring is going on”.

The petroleum minister, addressing the press briefing, said efforts were underway to ensure fuel availability.

“Today, I met with private oil refineries and discussed with them for one hour how to ensure that in September or October and even if any issues emerge in the Bab al-Mandab, how we can ensure fuel availability and distribute the burden evenly,” he said.

He said the government’s takeaway from the present situation should be that “it should be prepared to deal with such a crisis in the future”.

On the reduction in the petroleum levy, the minister referred to the relief scheme and said the government was taking steps to ease the fuel burden “despite buying fuel at twice the cost”.

Malik said the premier was personally supervising work on “strategic petroleum reserves, bonded schemes”.

He further said the targeted relief was estimated to cost roughly Rs25 billion a month, adding that “the federal government and the Ministry of Finance have given assurances”.

Free of charge registration message

Separately, PM Shehbaz chaired a meeting to review the progress on the relief scheme and directed that the message for the registration be made free of charge, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

The premier was briefed that more than 600,000 messages have been received from Islamabad since the launch of the scheme.

Out of the received messages, 42,933 applicants have been successfully registered for the PM Special Relief Scheme, the statement said.

The prime minister said the public should be provided with every possible guidance in registration and other necessary steps. He also ordered the launch of a comprehensive media awareness campaign regarding the scheme.

Finance minister approves fuel relief scheme

The cabinet’s Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) convened at the Finance Division on Monday for a meeting chaired by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, who approved PM Shehbaz’s fuel relief package.

According to a press release issued by the Finance Division, the ECC reviewed the Petroleum Division’s summary on the fuel relief scheme. Under the scheme, two- and three-wheelers will receive relief of Rs500 per week, equivalent to five litres at Rs100 per litre, while cars up to 800cc will receive Rs1,000 for 10 days, based on 30 litres per month at Rs100 per litre.

The plan will be restricted to non-commercial users, with relief limited to one vehicle per owner.

Meanwhile, the Ministry of IT and Telecom will deploy and manage the Fuel Pass System (FPS) for the digital management and transparent delivery of the scheme’s benefits.

“The targeted and digitally managed mechanism is aimed at ensuring that the benefit reaches eligible consumers efficiently while strengthening transparency and accountability in implementation,” the statement read, adding that the ECC approved a Rs75 billion technical supplementary grant to implement the scheme.

World.title: SC stresses need for gender-sensitive investigations, court proceedings in domestic violence cases
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court ruled on Monday that protecting women requires not only a shift in social attitudes but also the investigation and adjudication of domestic violence cases through a gender-sensitive lens.

“To effectively combat violence against women, the provincial governments must ensure that police officers receive appropriate training aimed at recognising and overcoming gender and patriarchal biases,” observed Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar in a 10-page judgment he authored regarding domestic homicide.

In domestic homicide, the tragedy is not only that a woman may be killed behind closed doors, it is that the doors may close upon the truth as well, Justice Kakar bemoaned, adding it was the job of the legal system to extract truth behind them.

Justice Kakar was heading a two-judge bench, including Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim, that had taken up a jail appeal of Habibullah, challenging the Nov 29, 2022 Sindh High Court (SHC) rejection of his plea. The appellant was convicted of murdering his wife, Aqeela Bibi, in Karachi in 2011.

The Supreme Court however upheld life sentence and a fine of Rs500,000 awarded to the appellant as compensation to the legal heirs of the deceased.

Justice Kakar emphasised that law enforcement agencies (LEAs) must adopt a genuinely gender-sensitive approach to investigation, ensuring that every available piece of evidence was duly identified, preserved and brought on record.

Likewise, the privacy of the matrimonial home should not be permitted to become a shield behind which perpetrators may evade accountability, and if any lapse happens due to negligence or a casual attitude of any investigating officer (IO), they must be held accountable.

Justice Kakar explained that certain offences belong to a special category of offences known to jurisprudence as a “Crime of Difficult Proof”, adding there were some crimes which were of frequent occurrence in society, and yet difficult to prove, like crimes committed inside the secrecy of homes such as infanticide or adultery.

Cases relating to domestic violence equally fall within this categorisation, including murder of a wife within the private bounds of her matrimonial home, Justice Kakar observed.

He added that such crimes could be termed as crimes of difficult proof primarily because they were committed inside closed, private structures such as a house, where the perpetrator enjoys complete physical control over the environment and also allows the perpetrator to easily destroy vital evidence, clean up the crime scene or stage the homicide to look like a suicide, accident, or intruder attack.
