Tech.title: TIFF 2026: The latest movie reviews from Toronto
Tech.content:
If you want an idea of what’s next in film, the Toronto International Film Festival is a good place to start. Every year TIFF features a huge range of features from around the world, and often some of them go on to be huge hits or awards contenders; the 2025 edition, for instance, included the likes of both Hamnet and Obsession.

Tech.title: macOS 27 is available now
Tech.content:
is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate on Monday, which brings the new Siri AI assistant, Liquid Glass improvements, improved performance, and more. The update is compatible with all Macs with Apple Silicon, but not Intel Macs — Apple released its final big update for Intel-based Macs last year with macOS Tahoe.

Siri AI is arguably the biggest feature in macOS 27, and it allows you to ask questions, search through things involving your personal context like photos and emails, and take actions in apps such as Messages and Reminders. There’s a new dedicated Siri app that keeps an archive of your chats for easier reference. However, Siri AI will initially launch as a beta and will only be available in English.

As for Liquid Glass, Apple says the update offers “uniform refraction and improved contrast,” and there is a new slider that makes Liquid Glass elements more or less opaque. And there’s one other major UI change worth celebrating: consistent window corner radii.

Tech.title: Apple releases iOS 27 with Siri AI overhaul
Tech.content:
Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Apple is now rolling out its iOS 27 update to compatible devices today, alongside the watchOS 27, iPadOS 27, and visionOS 27 updates. Siri AI is the headline feature across all four updates, the delayed AI-powered overhaul of the Siri assistant. Siri AI is available as a beta today for English-only devices, and Apple says support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish is coming in October.

Siri AI isn’t the only big feature in iOS 27, though. Apple is adding a new Liquid Glass opacity slider that lets you pick between a clearer UI or a more frosty one. A lot of built-in apps are also getting new icon designs, with subtle tweaks to colors, as well as extra large widgets and different volume settings for ringtones, alarms, timers, and alerts and system sounds.

watchOS 27 gets new Workout Buddy features, a new tap gesture, some Liquid Glass refinements, new Smart Stack suggestions, and an improved Find My app. Apple has also improved file transfer speeds to external drives on an iPad, sped up browsing on iPad, and added smoother connectivity moving between Wi-Fi and mobile data on iPads.

Apple Vision Pro users are also getting the Siri AI overhaul today as part of visionOS 27, as well as the ability to preview notifications by using your eyes, UI updates to the Control Center, improvements to Wi-Fi connectivity, and support for using the panoramas you’ve photographed as immersive scenes and environments.

Related macOS 27 is available now

The iOS 27 update will be available for iPhone 11 and iPhone SE (2nd gen) and later devices, with watchOS 27 available for Apple Watch SE 3, Apple Watch Series 9 and above, and Apple Watch Ultra 2 and above. iPadOS 27 is available for iPad Pro (4th generation and later, M1 and later), iPad Air (4th generation and later, M2 and later), iPad mini (6th generation, A17 Pro), and the base iPad (9th generation and later, A16).

Tech.title: The Steam Frame is made for irresponsible hardware nerds like me
Tech.content:
is a senior editor and founding member of The Verge who covers gadgets, games, and toys. He spent 15 years editing the likes of CNET, Gizmodo, and Engadget.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

For nearly three weeks, I’ve been testing the limits of Valve’s Steam Frame, the company’s new wearable PC. At first glance, it’s easy to write it off as a pricey headset that missed the VR craze. At $1,059 with 256GB of storage or $1,299 for 1TB, it costs two to three times as much as similar-looking headsets from Meta.

You should not write it off that way. The Steam Frame isn’t just a VR headset. It’s not even primarily a VR headset. And it’s the most comfortable headset I’ve ever worn. It weighs just over 1 pound (469g) with its optional top head strap attached, and doesn’t leave a mark on my face even after hours of use.

The Steam Frame is far more ambitious than VR alone. It’s an experimental attempt at a complete spatial computer that you can wear, not unlike the Apple Vision Pro, only here it’s aimed at gamers who want to play their flat library of Steam games plus the handful of VR titles on tap.

Pictured with optional $59 kit with hand straps and top third head strap; I highly recommend them.

No, if you write off the Steam Frame, it should be because you don’t want to pay $1,000-plus for early access hardware. Every day I spend with the Steam Frame, I feel like a beta tester. I’ve seen games crash so hard I needed to reboot the headset. I’ve had virtual objects, controls, and audio disappear. I’ve seen the entire device lose power more than once, its screen winking out right in front of my eyes.

But you should know I’m having so much fun. The Frame’s so comfortable that I don’t mind wearing it, and it feels like one of the most exciting betas I’ve ever tried. Like the Steam Deck at its debut, this is gadget nerd wish fulfillment. It’s a chance to watch Valve, one of the most intriguing companies in gaming, build a plane while flying it.

5 Verge Score Steam Frame $ 1059 $ 1059 The Good Lightweight and comfortable to wear

Precise wands double as a full gamepad

Plays so many games so many ways

Included 6GHz dongle allows short-range PC streaming even if you have questionable Wi-Fi The Bad Doesn’t feel like a finished product

Crashes, bugs, other assorted instability and inconsistencies

Not enough performance for many standalone games

Short battery life of one to two hours

Some audible fan noise $1059 at Valve How we rate and review products

The Steam Frame is primarily a gaming device. And it can certainly play games in a lot of different ways:

It can stream any flat or VR game from your Steam-equipped desktop or laptop.

It can play less demanding Windows games via emulation on its Arm-based Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 chip.

It can effectively be a Meta Quest , playing immersive VR games originally designed for Meta’s Android-based headsets.

natively designed for the Steam Frame’s Linux-on-Arm, too — like a new standalone version of the best single-player VR game, 2020’s It can play gamesfor the Steam Frame’s Linux-on-Arm, too — like a new standalone version of the best single-player VR game, 2020’s Half-Life: Alyx

And it can play mixed reality games where virtual objects seemingly float in your real world, as seen through the headset’s passthrough cameras.

It can do much of this because of the power of software — because Valve has spent years making games run where they didn’t originally belong.

But that’s just what it can do with games.

I am typing these words to you from virtual reality. I’m inside the Steam Frame surrounded by six virtual screens.

In front of me is Google Docs on effectively the largest computer monitor I’ve ever used, even counting the 48-inch TV that once lived atop my desk, and that screen is not alone. If I spin my office chair to the left, I’m facing my notes, calendar, and web browser. Spin it to the right, and there’s The Verge’s newsroom, my email, and a panel of Steam games. Above me, a Linux copy of Space Cadet Pinball waits to be played, while a YouTube window pipes in lo-fi music to help me focus.

Three of these screens are copies of my desktop PC’s three monitors, streaming from that PC, while the other three are running on the headset itself. I have Windows and Linux desktops running side by side in my own private world.

But whenever I try to explore all the possibilities I’ve just laid out, I quickly run into unexpected limitations, crashes, and bugs.

A peek at my multi-monitor Windows desktop inside the Steam Frame.

Let’s say I’m on my living room couch, and I want to stream a game from my PC that won’t easily run on the headset’s own chip, like the just-released Star Wars: Zero Company. The headset gives me a choice: I can launch the game in a window, or I can stream my entire PC desktop to the device.

I launch it in a window, then use the virtual laser pointers in Valve’s wand controllers to stretch the screen across my entire living room wall, while my wife sits next to me watching the BTS concert on my much smaller real-life TV on the same wall. I click the grip button on Valve’s wands one more time, and they begin emulating a full Xbox gamepad, with every button I need to play.

Valve’s virtual laser pointers are the primary way to navigate the UI; the headset can’t track your hands without the wands yet.

But suddenly, my streaming game is lagging and dropping frames like nobody’s business — because the Frame couldn’t decide whether to prioritize my home Wi-Fi or Valve’s included 6GHz wireless dongle, the company tells me later. My favorite seat on the living room couch is only about 12 feet and one wall away from the dongle, but that’s apparently the edge of its useful range. While Valve has “multi-link” streaming tech that could let the Frame balance both connections simultaneously, it currently only works when you’re streaming your entire PC.

Shall I try streaming my entire PC to the Steam Frame instead? But now I no longer feel like I’m hanging out with my wife, because the Frame’s passthrough cameras only work with streaming windows, not entire streaming PCs. The wands don’t work as a gamepad when streaming entire PCs, either. Nor do my Bluetooth keyboard and mouse when I pair them to the Frame.

Back in my virtual office, where I’m surrounded by six virtual screens, the same limitation means I don’t get to control them all simultaneously. I have to use my desktop mouse and keyboard to control the Windows screens, and my Steam Frame’s controls to control the Linux ones. The wands’ laser pointers can thankfully cross these boundaries, but sometimes I’ll click and nothing will happen.

When I try adding a seventh virtual screen, the Steam Frame chokes, and everything — all seven screens and the device’s entire user interface — spontaneously disappears. None of the buttons on my wands bring the UI back, so it’s time for a reboot again.

I’m not angry, and I don’t expect it’ll stay this way for long. But we can only review what’s in the box, and these are the kinds of things reviewers are currently experiencing.

When I set streaming aside and try playing games on its own Qualcomm chip, the Steam Frame has more power than I expect. There’s enough that I’d happily play VR games like Half-Life: Alyx from beginning to end on this device — fan-made Alyx mods are natively supported, too! — and I found myself getting sucked back into all kinds of lightweight flat games like Dave the Diver, Blue Prince, and Streets of Rage 4.

In terms of flat-screen gaming performance, it currently feels less powerful than the aging Steam Deck, with welterweight games like Hi-Fi Rush at the very edge of what I’m comfortable playing on its Qualcomm chip.

But here, I’m not constrained by a single 7-inch handheld screen, or even my 65-inch OLED TV. I’m backstabbing buddies in Super Battle Golf on a screen the size of my entire living room wall — while chatting with them in Discord on a second virtual screen that contains a full Linux desktop.

My Steam Deck handheld tops out at 1280 x 800 resolution, and by default, Valve locks flat Steam Frame games to a similar 1280 x 720. But the Frame’s LCD panels actually provide 2160 x 2160 per eye, and you can cram an incredible number of gaming pixels into that space if you try. The Frame can manage a game as old as 2007’s Portal at 2.8K resolution on a movie theater-sized virtual screen. There’s even a 5120 x 2880 option, though I haven’t found a single game weak enough to run that way.

The Frame controllers have every button, joystick, and trigger an Xbox gamepad does, in addition to VR controls.

Eye-tracking can help. By taking advantage of a technique called foveated rendering, games like Half-Life: Alyx and Dungeons of Eternity can spend more of their processing power producing sharp images where you’re actually looking while reducing resolution where you’re not. Dungeons of Eternity let me adjust the effect enough to tell it’s making a real difference. Red Matter 2 claims it’s providing an effective 4096 x 4096 resolution to my retinas, and I don’t doubt it: There’s a computer monitor early in the game whose glass screen is covered in lifelike scratches, and it looks incredible.

A flat 1080p screenshot really does not do it justice.

The Steam Frame doesn’t have dedicated Netflix or YouTube apps, but DRM content appears to work fine in the Chromium web browser: I’ve been watching full episodes of Peaky Blinders on Netflix almost every day at lunch. YouTube works in the browser (though not YouTube VR), and you can download VLC to watch all kinds of local video files. Speaking of streaming, you can stream your entire Sony PS5 to the Steam Frame with the Asobi app — I played some Yakuza that way.

I don’t always eat lunch in the Steam Frame, but when I do… …it’s small enough that there’s plenty of room.

And if you’re nerd enough to have 3D Blu-ray rips like me, Skybox is one of the excellent video players that’ll let you watch them in glorious 3D with convincing surround sound. Into the Spider-Verse looked amazing from my seat in a virtual movie theater, even though Steam Frame’s LCD displays don’t have the rich color of OLED. And Valve’s quad drivers sound remarkably good for something built into the frame of a headset.

But as of today, it’s tough to tell whether any given standalone app or game will run on the Steam Frame’s Arm chip — and run well — until you spend hours and gigabytes downloading and trying it for yourself.

You can even edit images in GIMP on the Linux desktop if you really want to.

Many just do, and it never ceases to wow me when I fire up, say, Fallout: New Vegas and the game actually launches on an entirely different operating system atop an entirely different processor architecture than its developers imagined. But some will launch and then take ages to load, like Shadow of the Tomb Raider, or fail to produce a visible image even though I can hear the game’s music, like Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time, or throw a major error on launch, like Doom: The Dark Ages.

Like with the Steam Deck, Valve will try to warn you first: It has a compatibility review program, badges for “Verified” and “Unsupported” games, and a dedicated “Great on Frame” store page so you can buy titles that should just work.

But the program’s in its infancy with just 130 “Verified” titles at the time I write the words, and even the badge is no guarantee a game will play perfectly. I was having a blast hacking and slashing skeletons in the Valve-verified Dungeons of Eternity for hours on end — but near the end of one dungeon, I suddenly lost audio and the ability to swing my club with my right controller. When I tried to throw my club at foes, it would just vanish.

The Steam Frame’s passthrough vision is monochrome, not color, though I’ll show you an accessory later that changes that.

Valve’s Jeremy Selan, one of the Steam Frame’s developers, suggests it won’t always be this way — I won’t always have to think about architectures and streaming technologies. I won’t always be bumping up against the seams.

“Our goal is that even though there’s a variety of ways to have these two computers talk to each other, we don’t want the user to have to think about ‘Am I streaming 2D? Am I streaming VR? Where are my controllers paired?’ We want every possible scenario to just work,” he says. “We’re going to try to make it where the device is just fun and seamless and you don’t have to think about those little things.”

He says I will “absolutely” be able to use the Steam Frame controllers as a gamepad for my entire remote PC, for example. That feature is already on the way and might even arrive by the time you read these words.

And he takes a moment to thank me for my bug reports. “No hyperbole: On my computer right now are the things you just mentioned, and those are my tasks for the next week.” He points out that Valve has already fixed a weird green line I saw underneath my streaming windows, and added the ability to make floating windows curved instead of flat, just two days after I asked for that.

I make almost all my windows curved, since they look crisper through the headset that way.

Selan admits that Valve does rely on early adopters to find issues, because the company’s own engineers “have become our own worst playtesters” after working on the headset for years. But he says that the way Valve works is to ship hundreds of updates to address user feedback. That’s what it did with the original Steam Controller and Steam Deck, and that’s what it sounds like he’s planning here.

I can’t think of a single company that’s ever supported hardware this way, but the Steam Deck went from a glorious mess to the easiest handheld gaming PC to recommend. Valve is still adding new features years later. And Valve has unified its software releases, so the Steam Machine (and soon Steam Frame) gets many of the same improvements.

The top feature he’d like to add to the Steam Frame is hand-tracking, he says, which is already working under the hood. (The controllers do per-finger sensing so you can have convincing virtual hands in games, but you can’t yet drop the wands and use your real hands instead.) And he’d like to get the Steam Machine streaming to the Steam Frame, a feature that won’t be available at launch.

“But we don’t get to work on those fun things until we make the device a joy for people who are new to it like yourself,” he tells me. Valve wants the bug reports to keep coming in.

The Steam Frame’s compute and optics are modular; Valve will release a different head strap in future with more battery and floating speakers. To remove the compute core, you technically need to undo three latches underneath the magnetic front cushion first.

If I’m being honest, I originally thought I’d spend most of this review comparing the Steam Frame to Meta’s Quest 3 and Quest 3S and the Apple Vision Pro. I figured I’d be talking about pancake versus Fresnel lenses, battery life, game selection, the fact that Valve’s headset doesn’t come with color passthrough cameras despite costing two to three times as much, the fact that Meta’s software is far more fleshed out.

Valve’s battery is small but makes for a comfortable curved rear headpiece, and I can route an external battery to it easily.

But here’s the simple truth: I don’t want to wear a Meta Quest or an Apple Vision Pro, because comfort trumps all. I own a Quest 2 and have access to the rest, but they all collect dust unless there’s a truly epic game to play — because they’re all front-heavy and put unwanted pressure on my face.

When it comes to comfort, the Steam Frame mops the floor with anything else I’ve tried. It doesn’t leave a red ring around my face. In fact, it can float so freely on my face that I don’t need to keep the Frame’s silky cushions attached — I can remove the rear one for less bulk against pillows and headrests, a trick that Selan says he sometimes uses in bed.

(The optional top head strap is part of a $59 accessories kit, though it also includes Valve’s excellent “Knuckles”-style hand straps and so I think it’s worth the money.)

The only thing I find uncomfortable about the Frame is that it gets warm enough to trigger an audible fan, but at least it’s a tolerable “whoosh” sound (not a whine) and it keeps my face cool by sending in fresh air.

Ask me anything! Do you have a burning question about the Steam Frame that I didn’t answer in this review? I’m holding a subscriber-only AMA at 4PM ET today (that’s 1PM PT for me!). If you get your questions in early, I might even be able to test new things for you!

And while the Frame’s 21.6-watt-hour battery doesn’t last long — heavy games can last less than an hour, and I’ve yet to see more than two hours in its battery-saving mode or while streaming — its rear-mounted USB-C port is well placed to route a cable down to a battery in my pocket. Even my tiny 36Wh Iniu battery gave me an entire extra hour of play, and my old 100Wh HyperJuice battery lasted an entire 2.5-hour session of Dungeons of Eternity while charging up the Steam Frame, too.

You can effortlessly add color passthrough to the Frame if you want, by the way — Arcturus, which helped build the Frame’s entire vision system, is now selling a perfect-fit 5K60 10-bit HDR stereo camera for $150. Just shove it into the Frame’s nose bridge port and the headset’s monochrome passthrough vision automatically changes to color, because Valve baked in native support. It’s clear enough that I can read my phone’s screen, something you can’t do without, and it lets you record spatial video clips.

Adding the Arcturus Vision Camera. Installation: Just press up with one thumb.

That said, Valve’s stock infrared camera system has charm — when I need a glass of water in the middle of the night, it’s fun to walk around with what’s effectively a night vision headset on.

The Arcturus camera isn’t the only modular component coming for the Steam Frame, by the way. The entire compute core of the Frame is detachable so you can connect it to other head strap, audio, and battery solutions instead, and Valve is planning one of its own: An “Enthusiast Kit” will come with a new head strap that lets you stack a second magnetic battery pack onto the first one to double the Frame’s battery capacity, a premium set of off-ear floating speakers based on the Valve Index Ear Speakers, and additional eye spacers that can get you even closer to (or farther from) its lenses.

No price, release date, or photos of that one just yet.

I can’t imagine the Steam Frame will be anywhere near as much of a success as the Steam Deck. It costs so much more, and it requires people to wear a gadget on their face. That’s why most of these headsets have always been a hard sell.

But the Frame doesn’t cost quite as much as I feared it might, and it finally lets game developers target a consumer wireless headset that isn’t ultimately controlled by Mark Zuckerberg, or any of the other companies that tried headsets but don’t seem to care as much anymore. But even if you don’t want to play VR games, even if you believe VR is dead for now, there are all kinds of intriguing things to do with a Linux desktop and a catalog of flat-screen Steam games on your head.

If you’re the kind of nerd who’d love that, I don’t want to scare you away. The Steam Deck was a mess at launch, but it was also so much fun. Sometimes becoming a beta tester isn’t such a bad thing.

Tech.title: OpenAI buys smartphone camera maker Glass Imaging for $300 million, report says
Tech.content:
In Brief

OpenAI has bought smartphone camera maker Glass Imaging in a deal worth over $300 million, according to a report from the Wall Street Journal. The company, founded in 2019 and based in Los Altos, California, had previously raised about $30 million in funding from investors.

Glass Imaging was founded by Ziv Attar and Tom Bishop, a pair of former Apple engineers who previously led the team that developed Apple’s Portrait Mode. This background directly informs the work they now do at Glass Imaging, where they use AI to overcome the physical size constraints of smartphone cameras. Rather than using AI to edit a photo after it’s been taken, Glass Imaging uses neural networks to learn about individual camera systems — like the different cameras on various smartphone models — to yield better images from the moment the shutter clicks.

OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The ChatGPT maker is rumored to be working on its own hardware, like smartphones, earbuds, and AI companion devices.

In 2025, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and famed Apple designer Jony Ive revealed that they had been working together on a device startup called io, when OpenAI bought Ive’s company for $6.5 billion.

Tech.title: AI infrastructure company Cornelis raises $205M to chip away at Nvidia’s dominance
Tech.content:
In Brief

Cornelis, a company creating networking technology to help AI chips communicate more effectively, announced Monday that it has raised $205 million in a funding round led by IAG Capital Partners.

It also announced a product called Active Compute Fabric, a network technology that targets the fact that much GPU time is wasted waiting for data to arrive. Cornelis hopes to address this with a networking fabric that lets chips process and send information at the same time.

The company, which spun off from Intel in 2020, is competing with Nvidia by offering an open architecture, meaning customers can use a variety of GPU and accelerator hardware with Cornelis’ networking fabric. Though Nvidia chips can technically run on other networking fabrics, they’re optimized to run on Nvidia’s own software, making it much easier — and more enticing — for customers to use Nvidia’s full GPU stack. Cornelis is part of a new wave of AI infrastructure companies emerging to break apart Nvidia’s market dominance, piece by piece (or chip by chip, one could say).

Cornelis has already started shipping its product and is working on a new generation of it, expected to be released later this year.

Tech.title: Amazon Prime Video takes on TikTok with short-form news clips
Tech.content:
Amazon Prime Video is coming after TikTok with the addition of short-form news clips. The company said on Monday that it’s expanding its news coverage to include on-demand news clips offering both local and national stories. These will be available on TVs and other living room devices, but will soon roll out to the web and Prime Video’s mobile apps, the company said.

The clips will be available in the News destination within the Prime Video app in its Trending Topics and the Local News carousels. They join Prime Video’s existing local, national, and world news coverage from a number of major providers, which are available to everyone in the U.S. regardless of whether they have a Prime subscription.

Amazon could not yet confirm whether the clips on mobile would be oriented for vertical video or not, only that they would be considered short-form content on iOS and Android.

While TikTok is better known as an entertainment destination, it’s also, along with Instagram, increasingly a place where younger people get their news. Gen Z in particular often watches news creators and influencers on short-form apps, including YouTube Shorts. Amazon, which doesn’t have a true social destination of its own, is instead adding short-form video to Prime Video, in hopes of capturing Gen Z’s attention.

But Gen Z viewers are drawn to these social apps not necessarily because of the length of the clips, but rather because of how the information is presented. Based on findings from Pew Research, these younger news consumers want short-form news content that “feels organic, not over-produced.”

Prime Video is not the first streamer to add short-form clips to its content lineup. Peacock added support for short-form clips in March, followed by HBO Max and Netflix in July, then Disney+ in August. Combined, the updates represent an industrywide effort to meet viewers where they are — which is now often looking for entertainment in shorter bursts and consumable in moments or minutes instead of portions of hours or longer.

Tech.title: ClickFix attacks are tricking Mac and Windows users into hacking themselves
Tech.content:
If you clicked on an HBO Max ad on Reddit over the past week, you might want to check your computer for malware.

These so-called “ClickFix” attacks have quickly become one of the rising cybersecurity threats of 2026, and they’re getting both sneakier and compromising people’s devices with greater frequency. Until recently, ClickFix attacks were a rarity, capitalizing on people searching the web for quick tech fixes. They have since evolved into a massive international effort to hack into people’s computers.

The attacks involve fake websites, or legitimate websites that have been hacked, which display a message that appears to look like a CAPTCHA or an anti-bot checkbox. Once clicked, a prompt appears asking the user to perform a “check” to proceed, which gives instructions to copy and paste a string of text into the user’s Windows command prompt or Mac Terminal app.

As soon as the user hits return, they unwittingly and instantly install info-stealing malware on their computer, capable of immediately stealing their passwords, access to their logged-in accounts, and crypto wallets. Since the user is working in the computer’s terminal, which lets them interact directly with the operating system using text-based commands, many of these attacks evade antivirus and security defense tools.

Security researchers now say that the latest ClickFix campaign they’ve seen involved hackers posting fake ads on Reddit, linking to a page that looks like HBO Max but contains a ClickFix lure that tricks people into hacking themselves. The hackers compromised the official HBO Max’s account on Reddit that was then used to post hundreds of fake but real-looking adverts to the news-sharing site, according to security researchers at Hudson Rock and a thread on Reddit’s cybersecurity subreddit.

It’s unclear how many people clicked on these fake ads or how many were ultimately compromised as a result. Warner Brothers Discovery, which owns HBO, did not respond to a request for comment.

Reddit told TechCrunch it “recently learned that an HBO Max account authorized to run s on Reddit was compromised and used to run ads containing malicious links,” and that the company locked the account and removed the ads. When asked, Reddit did not say how many users were targeted or clicked the malicious ads.

While it’s typical for developers to run one-line snippets of code in their computer’s terminal, it’s less common for regular users to use the Command Prompt or PowerShell in Windows, or the Terminal in macOS. Companies that run fleets of Windows computers can block access to these features across the entire domain to prevent them from being exploited, per security researcher Kevin Beaumont.

As noted by Ars Technica, a tool for Mac users called BlockBlock can also defend against attacks that try to trick Apple users into hacking themselves.

Updated with comment from Reddit.

Tech.title: Volkswagen’s crazy-efficient EV borrows an idea from Slate
Tech.content:
Volkswagen took the covers off a new prototype electric vehicle Monday, one that’s capable of hitting the equivalent of 323 miles per gallon under ideal conditions, making it one of the most efficient cars in the world.

It’s not unusual for automakers to float pie-in-the-sky concepts with outlandish stats, but Volkswagen took it a step or two further by building the EV and driving it from its home base in Wolfsburg, Germany, on a 794-mile (1,278-kilometer) trip to Vienna. The team charged the Mission Efficiency prototype once during the journey and arrived with 104 miles (168 kilometers) of range left, resulting in consumption of 7.51 kilowatt-hours per 100 miles, or about 279 MPGe.

Volkswagen actually built and drove the Mission Efficiency prototype Image Credits:Volkswagen

The teardrop-shaped Mission Efficiency prototype was built using the electric motor and battery from the ID. Polo, two features that bring the car to “near production” status, Volkswagen said in a press release.

For those keeping score, the prototype is almost twice as efficient as the most efficient production car in the world, the Lucid Air Pure.

By some back-of-the-envelope math, Volkswagen’s science experiment can get more than 400 miles of range out of a 54.9-kilowatt-hour battery, though that’s not an official EPA rating. Lucid gets 420 miles from an 84-kilowatt-hour battery per EPA ratings, but it’s a much larger and more practical vehicle.

Volkswagen had to make some compromises in the name of efficiency.

The most noticeable is the roofline, which tapers quickly after peaking above the driver’s head. The shape, known as a Kammback, is among the most aerodynamic shapes a vehicle can take. Volkswagen was able to bring the coefficient of drag down to 0.158, while also keeping the frontal area low at just 2.08 square meters.

Being a 2+2, the Mission Efficiency’s back seat is suitable for children, maybe Image Credits:Volkswagen

As a result, the Mission Efficiency is technically a 2+2, meaning the rear seats aren’t suitable for most adults. Volkswagen said the backseat is designed for people shorter than 5-foot 3 inches, or about 1.6 meters.

“The prototype was designed so that it could theoretically be used by a young family of four,” Volkswagen said, though anyone who has contemplated sitting in a 2+2 knows that even kids might scoff at the notion.

Another compromise sits closer to the road. Because wheels and tires can contribute about a quarter to a third of aerodynamic drag, the designers tightened the space between the wheel arches and the front tires. It’s great for efficiency, but probably not great for ride quality since wheels need space to move inside the wheel wells so the shocks can absorb bumps.

Volkswagen included some clever touches, including this storage bin that’s hidden behind the rear wheel cover Image Credits:Volkswagen

One place Volkswagen didn’t compromise was the mirrors. Sideview mirrors generate a lot of drag just by hanging off the sides, and while cameras would have cut into those losses significantly, they don’t offer the same sense of depth that true mirrors do.

To top it all off, Volkswagen put solar cells on the roof and the trunk lid. It’s a nice touch that’s sure to delight the internet, but their impact is limited, adding just 18 miles (30 kilometers) to perfectly flat, sunny routes driven at a constant 42.25 mph (68 kph).

Like the Slate EV pickup, the Mission Efficiency doesn’t come with an infotainment system Image Credits:Volkswagen

Inside, the seats are built using lightweight materials and designs. On the dash, Volkswagen took a page from EV startup Slate Auto. Like Slate’s bare-bones pickup, the Mission Efficiency doesn’t come with an infotainment system or built-in speakers. Instead, it offers a portable Bluetooth speaker and assumes drivers will bring their own devices.

While Volkswagen frequently calls the Mission Efficiency a “near production” vehicle, the company didn’t commit to actual production. Though don’t assume it won’t: Over a decade ago, the automaker produced 250 examples of the XL1, another efficiency-minded halo car. And like other halo cars, it didn’t come cheap, with prices starting at €110,000 in 2013.

Tech.title: With iOS 27, I’m actually using Siri again
Tech.content:
For years, I barely used Siri for anything beyond menial tasks like setting timers or alarms. That has changed with iOS 27, as I now repeatedly use Siri for complex requests and to make sense of on-screen context.

While Siri is clearly front and center in this software update by Apple, I also enjoy many of the other quality-of-life updates.

Siri

I have been using iOS 27 on my main device since the public beta version was released, and on another device through the developer beta before that. I have really enjoyed using the new Siri, often trying to find new use cases for it — and that’s possibly the biggest win for Apple, given that I, like many people, had given up on Siri before this update.

Over two years ago, Apple introduced Apple Intelligence and teased an advanced version of Siri. And after multiple delays, the company is finally shipping it, and it doesn’t disappoint. Built on the back of Google’s Gemini models, Siri is much smarter than its previous version, which was built on extended knowledge and a shaky ChatGPT integration. It also has a new logo and transition animation.

For starters, I asked Siri about several different things in the area of sports, ranging from World Cup matches to team lineups and scores. There were some hiccups in the earlier developer versions, but most of the information was correct. Siri can also take complex, multistep directions. For instance, I asked it to find small or hidden and useful features for iOS 27 and add them to a note, and it did a good job of that.

Plus, Siri can draft a message for you and send it to someone.

And because Siri can fetch context from your files, messages, and email, you can also ask it to look up a conversation, like one related to a delivery, and have it create a message for returns.

Image Credits:TechCrunch (screenshot)

Siri’s on-screen context was a big blessing, too. I could ask trivial questions like who was the oldest player on the pitch when I was looking at lineups for two teams in the World Cup, or have it read the text on-screen out loud when I didn’t want to read. When I was on a startup’s website, I could ask Siri to look up its funding information and competitors.

One of my favorite use cases was surfing around coffee Reddit for new roasters and beans, and asking Siri to add it to a specific note. I did face a few difficulties in getting Siri to add it to the right note, but eventually I dumbed down the note’s name for better consistency.

The Camera app also now has Siri access, which means you can ask questions about things that are visible in your viewfinder. When I was at a restaurant, I asked Siri what drink I was holding. Because of the color of the drink, it said, “This is green juice,” which is a good first visual assumption. When I specified that I was at an Indian restaurant, it correctly said this could be Jaljeera or Aam Panna. (It was the latter.) I also took a photo of the restaurant’s sign and asked Siri to suggest the best items from its menu.

You can also take a photo of a coffee bag and ask Siri for the best way to brew the coffee.

Image Credits:Ivan Mehta

With iOS 27, Siri AI gets a dedicated app that lets you return to your previous chats. In Settings, users can change Siri’s voice and expressiveness, as well.

The new assistant is positioned to work with other, third-party apps, and as developers update their apps after the operating system rolls out, it will be interesting to see if there is a smooth handoff between Siri and apps.

Image Credits:TechCrunch (screenshot)

Apple Intelligence

Apple Intelligence powers a number of AI features in iOS 27.

For instance, Apple has sprinkled vibe-coding features within the new OS. The first is a Shortcuts creation feature that lets you describe shortcuts and automations in natural language to create them. That means you can start with a simple request, like “Show me today’s to-do items every morning at 8 a.m.” or “convert photo to JPEG,” instead of having to figure out how to craft the shortcut yourself. After the shortcut is created, you can make it more complex by adding more steps, like “convert selected photos to JPEG and share them through AirDrop.”

I always wanted to create a list of songs that I heard and liked in bars and cafes, so I made a shortcut to Shazam the song and save both the track and location.

You can also now create a custom alert in Safari to track changes to a page like a blog, item pricing, or a privacy policy page.

The Photos app has some new handy tools like “reframe” and “extend.” I found they don’t always work that well, but in some cases, they can make an image look better. Meanwhile, Apple has definitely improved its eraser functionality, which now leaves fewer strange artifacts when you remove an object.

Image Credits: Ivan Mehta Image Credits:Ivan Mehta Image Credits: Ivan Mehta Image Credits:Ivan Mehta

With Apple Intelligence, when you get certain messages such as information for an event or location, smart suggestions will ask if you’d like to add them to your Calendar or Notes. What’s more, the Passwords app can now automatically change passwords on your behalf by logging into a site.

Other quality-of-life improvements

Before discussing any other features, I have to say that I love the new clipboard feature. This lets you paste anything — including links, photos, videos, and text — from one app to another easily. Once the item is in your clipboard, you see a shortcut button saying “paste from Safari” (or similar) on the keyboard, which lets you paste the item. I have been using this feature frequently, and I can’t stress enough how life-changing this is despite it being a small change.

Image Credits:Screenshot by TechCrunch

In addition, iOS 27 addresses people’s gripes about the look of Liquid Glass. Users can now change its transparency based on their preferences. The control is granular, so you don’t have to choose from presets, either.

Apple also introduced intelligent network switching in this update, which automatically flips the connection from Wi-Fi to mobile data if there are issues with the wireless connection. The switching is seamless and very handy when you are doing important work, so you don’t lose your internet connection.

The update focuses a lot on child safety as well, as it includes a new setup flow that automatically recommends essential apps. Plus, parents can set schedules, time limits, and allowances for different days of the week. Guardians can get notifications when children are accessing new websites and can approve that access remotely. And the system displays a warning when children are exposed to nudity in Messages, FaceTime, and other apps.

Image Credits:Apple

Besides Siri AI, iOS 27 doesn’t have many marquee features, but it makes everyday life much easier. In previous years, I would have defaulted to going to ChatGPT or Gemini to get answers for a question. But with iOS 27, I find myself using Siri more often, even though I don’t live in Apple’s Messages and Mail apps.

iOS 27 is rolling out to all users with iPhone 11 or later and iPhone SE (second gen) or later. Users can go to Settings > General > Software Update to download the latest version.

Tech.title: macOS 27: new Siri takes on AI productivity apps
Tech.content:
The two most noticeable things about macOS 27 Golden Gate are the newly updated Siri AI and the design changes that make windows and icons more consistent. Siri AI offers the same features and capabilities as on iOS 27, but the Mac gives it access to different context — and new ways to be useful.

Over the last few years, apps and browsers have tried to learn more about your work and what you want to use AI assistants for, so they can better answer your questions or perform tasks. Today, many top web browsers, excluding Safari, come with a sidebar-based AI assistant that can look at one or multiple open tabs to provide contextual answers. Apps like Highlight, Caddy, and Littlebird can also look at your current window, then use that information as context for your queries.

The new Siri is similar. You can invoke Siri anywhere on your screen, allowing it to answer questions about what it sees, summarize information, or provide you with more details. For instance, if you are looking at an item you want to purchase, you could ask Siri to show you alternative options too.

Instead of having Siri look at the whole page, you can also select a part of the page via Apple’s new Visual Intelligence features. If you press Command + Shift + Space, you can add the currently focused window to your context for the AI.

To select a specific part, press Command + Shift + 6 to bring up a crosshair selection tool. After this, you can directly ask a question or perform an image search. Based on your selection, you will also get shortcuts like “Select,” “Add to Contact,” and “Look up Location.”

Image Credits:Ivan Mehta

Apple has also improved Spotlight Search on Mac. You can directly ask Siri questions within Spotlight to get answers from the web, and now you can also select Applications, Files, Actions, and Clipboard to search within that particular area of context. Plus, Spotlight now allows you to run Shortcuts or look up your recent search history.

Since Siri has access to your files, emails, and messages, you can search for a variety of things that you couldn’t before. In tests, I pulled up membership IDs without opening my files, asked for details about an upcoming trip, and looked up the embargo date for an upcoming news story in the works. While I don’t find Spotlight as advanced as the highly extensible Mac productivity tool Raycast, it’s still much better than before.

Image Credits:Ivan Mehta

Siri can also now help you with reviewing documents or performing writing tasks. Since the desktop is one of the better surfaces for writing long text, I found it to be more useful here than on the iPhone. You can do things like select a block of text and ask Siri to proofread it, improve it, or rewrite it. You can also ask Siri to draft something for you within any text box.

Safari, meanwhile, has added AI-powered page tracking, which is useful for keeping an eye on things like price drops, privacy policy changes, or new blog posts on pages when there is no RSS support. Plus, Safari can automatically organize tabs based on topics, which is handy.

Image Credits:Ivan Mehta

One small but neat new feature is that when you download a file or rename it, the system suggests a name based on context in the Finder or when you’re saving the document.

Apart from Siri, macOS 27 Golden Gate brings design changes with new Liquid Glass icons, an adjustable slider for the Liquid Glass design, and a better way to “diffuse” content when you move windows around.

The company said that app windows have a more consistent corner radius. Sidebars now stretch edge to edge and have new colorful icons. The new operating system update also better highlights active windows.

The OS update additionally adds features like enhanced child safety controls, shared cross-platform photo albums, and an updated eraser, better search in email, app resizing for iPhone mirroring, and quick suggestions for adding events to the calendar.

Starting today, macOS 27 Golden Gate is available for MacBook Air and MacBook Pro 2020 versions with Apple Silicon or later, iMac with Apple Silicon (2021 or later), Mac Mini (2020 or later), Mac Studio (2022 or later), Mac Pro (2023 or later), and MacBook Neo. Go to System Settings > General > Software Update to get the latest version.

Tech.title: Fashion app Daydream uses Apple Intelligence to help you shop the outfits in your camera roll
Tech.content:
Daydream, an AI-powered fashion discovery app, launched two new features on Monday to let iPhone users turn saved outfit photos into shoppable results and search for clothing and accessories through Siri, without opening the app.

The new features were built using Apple’s iOS 27 developer tools, which officially rolled out today. To use either feature, you’ll need an iPhone running iOS 27 with Siri AI enabled, along with the Daydream app installed. The app is free to download on iOS devices.

The first feature uses Apple’s image-context capabilities, letting users shop from images already saved in their Photos app. Daydream analyzes the outfit in the image, identifies its individual pieces, and automatically surfaces shoppable matches and similar styles from Daydream’s catalog of roughly 3 million products.

Image Credits:Daydream

That means a screenshot of an outfit found on Instagram or Pinterest could become the starting point for a shopping search. Daydream can break down the image into relevant items, such as a sweater, pants, shoes, or accessories, and match them with products available through its collection. If the exact item in the photo is still available, Daydream can match the image back to the retailer selling it. If it’s no longer available, the app will instead surface similar options.

It can also handle requests for variations on what appears in an image. “I like this sweater but want it in red,” for example, is the kind of request Daydream can understand, Julie Bornstein, co-founder and CEO of Daydream, explained to TechCrunch.

The second feature is a Siri-powered natural-language search function. Users can make requests by voice or text through Siri without having to open Daydream’s app.

A user could say, “Hey, Siri, search Daydream for a cool blazer for my board meeting on Monday,” and Daydream then provides results personalized to them.

Bornstein adds that the experience can be more tailored if users have set up Daydream’s “Style Passport,” which asks for details such as their sizes, preferred brands, personal style, and budget.

Image Credits:Daydream

The company joins a growing number of AI shopping tools designed to rethink product discovery, such as big names like Google and Amazon, as well as some smaller players like Onton and Alta. But Bornstein believes that Daydream’s latest features offer something special that a lot of these other tools just can’t match.

“Most visual search tools don’t have the fashion category expertise, so they return results that don’t feel accurate, from brands that aren’t credible, or they link you to nonshoppable images,” she said.

The launch fits into Daydream’s broader bet on AI-powered fashion shopping. The company sees these new features as more than stand-alone shopping tools. Its longer-term ambition is to build a shopping agent.

“This is one step toward the bigger vision, [which is] a shopping agent that understands someone’s style well enough to work across every surface in their life, not just on one surface,” Bornstein said. “Expect us to keep going deeper into on-device intelligence and further into the everyday moments where people are already discovering things they want.”

Daydream’s app launched last year and touts that it has more than 1.5 million shoppers browsing products from more than 325 retailers and 10,000 brands. Its retail lineup includes brands such as Anthropologie, Dolce & Gabbana, Uniqlo, J.Crew, Reformation, Gucci, and Nordstrom.

Tech.title: The Top New Features in Apple’s iOS 27 and iPadOS 27
Tech.content:
Apple's latest iPhone and iPad software—iOS 27 and iPadOS 27—is here. While this release won’t make as big of a splash as Apple’s big Liquid Glass redesign in the prior version, there's still plenty here that could change how you use your device.

iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 focus largely on stability improvements that you’ll notice in your everyday use. There are several quality-of-life improvements, like how Shortcuts are significantly easier to set up, but the big highlight is the Siri AI upgrade. Here's everything you need to know.

Updated September 14, 2026: We've refreshed this story to reflect the latest updates and that iOS and iPadOS 27 are rolling out today.

Is Your iPhone or iPad Compatible? AccordionItemContainerButton LargeChevron Apple sometimes drops a few older devices from the support list with new versions of its operating systems, supposedly because the aging hardware can’t run the latest screen behaviors without feeling sluggish. (Apple typically supports iPhones and iPads for six to seven years.) But there's good news this year. iPhones from 2019 and newer—the iPhone 11 and up, including the iPhone SE (2nd Gen)—will support iOS 27. That means any iPhone that received iOS 26 is still compatible with iOS 27. If you're unsure of your iPhone model, go to Settings > General > About and look at the model name. iPads aren't as straightforward, as they have a unique naming structure. Apple retired the “generations” moniker and is now using the chipset to denote the iPad model. You can check your iPad model using Apple’s support documentation. A few iPads are cut off from the iPadOS 27 update, including the 8th-gen iPad from 2020 and the 5th-gen iPad Mini. iPad : 9th gen and later, including A16

: 9th gen and later, including A16 iPad Mini : 6th gen and later, including A17 Pro

: 6th gen and later, including A17 Pro iPad Air 11-inch : 4th gen and later, including M2, M3, and M4

: 4th gen and later, including M2, M3, and M4 iPad Air 13-inch: M2 and later

M2 and later iPad Pro 11-inch : 2nd gen and later

: 2nd gen and later iPad Pro 12.9-inch: 4th gen and later

4th gen and later iPad Pro: M4 and later How to Install iOS 27 or iPadOS 27 AccordionItemContainerButton LargeChevron The final versions of iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 are here. Before installing, it’s very important that you back up your devices. Head to Settings, tap your name at the top, and select iCloud. Then tap iCloud Backup, and tap Back Up Now. Read our How to Back Up Your iPhone or iPad guide for other methods and more details. Then, head to Settings > General > Software Update and choose iOS 27 or iPadOS 27 when you see the option. Installation will take several minutes, and your iPhone or iPad will restart, so set aside several minutes for the whole process. Siri AI, the new assistant, will ask to index your phone or iPad to learn more about you, your apps, and your data so it can be more helpful. This indexing takes a while—anywhere from a few hours to a couple of days—so be prepared to wait a bit. Apple Intelligence Only Works on Select iPhones AccordionItemContainerButton LargeChevron Remember—even if older iPhones and iPads receive the iOS 27 or iPadOS 27 update, that doesn't mean all of the new features will be available. Apple Intelligence is still only compatible with the iPhone 15 Pro and newer and select iPads, meaning that several artificial intelligence features are unavailable on older devices.

Top New iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 Features

Here's a top-line view of some of the biggest changes coming to iOS and iPadOS 27. The updates are largely the same across both operating systems.

Siri AI and a New Siri App

Courtesy of Apple

Siri is finally becoming “a more capable assistant,” or so Apple claims. The company says this is largely thanks to its third-generation foundation models, developed from the ground up with Google's Gemini models. However, Apple says it isn't using Google's infrastructure to power Siri interactions and that no user data from Siri actions gets shared with Google.

Siri AI has an all-new look when you activate the assistant. It now resembles a glass orb. You can type or talk naturally to Siri, and there's even a dedicated Siri app where you can revisit previous conversations or pick up where you left off on a different device. Siri is also now in the camera app, giving you a more direct way to start a visual search, much like Google Lens. You can even point the camera at a restaurant bill, and Siri can split the tab between you and your friends.

The assistant understands your personal context, so it can comb through your emails, messages, and photos to find relevant information based on your query. It can then take action on your behalf, whether that's drafting an email in a specific tone or getting wine recommendations for a particular dish. Siri's voice is more expressive, but you can also customize the assistant's voice, its expressiveness, and its pace.

We've collated all the new things you can do with Siri AI if you want to try the revamped assistant.

Platform Stability Improvements

Courtesy of Apple

Apple has focused on making iOS run faster in this update. The company says app launches are up to 30 percent faster, newly captured photos in your Photo Library load up to 70 percent faster, and AirDrop transfers are up to 80 percent faster. The iPhone will do a better job switching between Wi-Fi and cellular, so you hopefully won't have that awkward minute with no service while you wait for your device to switch networks as you leave the house. Many of these upgrades will affect older iPhone models, like the iPhone 11, thanks to a better-optimized CPU Scheduler.

Liquid Glass Refinements

Courtesy of Apple

Hate Liquid Glass? Love Liquid Glass? You have some options to make it work for your tastes in iOS 27. Apple says it has generally updated the design language to improve readability and contrast. App icons are sharper, for example. But you now finally have a slider in the Settings menu that lets you adjust the intensity of the Liquid Glass look, from super clear to more opaque. You can customize this in Settings > Appearance > Liquid Glass.

Child Safety Features

Courtesy of Apple

Apple spent a lot of time in the WWDC keynote talking up child safety features in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27. A new Setup Assistant lets parents choose system apps and other essential apps for the child when first setting up an Apple device. An Ask to Browse feature means any new websites the kids encounter in Safari get sent to a parent for approval, and a feature called Communication Safety prevents children from seeing nudity or violence in the Messages or FaceTime apps; those are blurred by default.

Tech.title: New York Seizes a Dozen Celebrity Deepfake Websites
Tech.content:
For the best part of a decade, abusive deepfake “pornography” websites have published thousands of nonconsensual videos depicting women, including high-profile celebrities, politicians, and public figures, into sexual situations. Now, in what is likely the largest takedown of explicit deepfake websites to date, officials in New York have seized more than a dozen of the harmful sites.

On Monday, the Manhattan District Attorney’s Office announced the seizure of 12 domains which it says have been used for “unlawfully” sharing, publishing, and selling celebrity deepfake videos. Around 1,200 people—overwhelmingly women—were depicted in nonconsensual sexual images and videos on the websites, the office says. These included social media influencers, actors, activists, athletes, musicians, and politicians.

“These horrific violations of privacy follow victims into their careers and personal lives and take an immense toll on emotional and mental well-being,” district attorney Alvin Bragg said in a statement, urging potential victims to come forward and contact his office’s cybercrime bureau. The office says its investigations into who is responsible for the websites, plus those who uploaded damaging videos of victims, are ongoing.

The seizures, carried out under New York’s criminal procedure laws, mark perhaps one of the most significant and sweeping actions against websites hosting explicit deepfake videos since the technology first emerged at the end of 2017. As artificial intelligence technology has improved, a dark industry of websites, apps, and bots has appeared: They are designed to “undress” photos of women or create graphic sexual videos that include them. The images and videos are increasingly realistic and can be generated in seconds.

While deepfake technology is widely used against non-famous women and girls—often being shared in private social media groups—celebrities have spoken out about the many harms of being depicted in the content and the challenges of getting it removed. While laws against deepfakes have been slow to emerge, the US Take It Down Act increasingly allows images to be removed, with part of the law allowing law enforcement officials to take down and seize websites.

The Manhattan District Attorney’s Office has not publicly named the websites it has seized. However, ahead of Bragg’s announcement, WIRED independently observed several of the sites’ homepages being replaced by takedown notices—“THIS DOMAIN HAS BEEN SEIZED”—late last week, with the sites now saying they have been taken over following a seizure warrant issued by a New York State Supreme Court.

“The takedowns are a significant win in the fight against synthetic nonconsensual intimate imagery (NCII),” says Leonie Oehmig, a researcher at the Institute for Strategic Dialogue (ISD), who has studied the deepfake creation ecosystem. Oehmig says that enforcement of state laws shows that the harmful content can be tackled and that the seized sites don’t appear to be accessible if using VPNs to try and access them from other locations. “This shows that meaningful, coordinated enforcement is achievable even where regulation itself remains fragmented across jurisdictions.”

The websites were likely viewed millions of times. Many used names that included phrases such as “sex celebrity” or promised “real deepfakes.” They hosted false videos of some of the world’s most famous celebrities, with one saying, “various actresses’ faces are used for deepfakes.”

Videos could be several minutes in length and include fully sexually explicit scenes—often swapping the faces of celebrities or public figures into existing pornographic videos. Archived versions of the websites show some videos had been watched tens of thousands of times, with one of the websites claiming to have been online since 2018.

Tech.title: The Best Air Purifier of 2026: Tested Picks for Every Room
Tech.content:
The Levoit Vital 200S-P Air Purifier cleared smoke and got the air back to a healthy level in four minutes and 15 seconds. Video: Molly Higgins The Coway Airmega Mighty2 cleared smoke and got the air back to a healthy level in four minutes and 10 seconds. Video: Molly Higgins

The IQAir HealthPro Plus XE never even allowed the smoke pellet pollutants to visually cloud the tent. The AQI and PM 2.5 levels were marked as “hazardous,” but within three minutes the levels were back to “good.” Video: Molly Higgins The Shark BreatheClear Max didn’t auto-adjust to the pollutants like others tested, and smoke didn’t visually clear. I had to restart the purifier and it took almost five hours for the monitor to read that it was at a healthy level again. Video: Molly Higgins

Compare Our Picks

Others Tested

Photograph: Molly Higgins

Shark BreatheClear Max for $360: Launched in April (we've previously tested the Shark NeverChange Air Purifier and Shark NeverChange Air Purifier Max), this purifier offers intelligent purification that automatically adjusts fan speed in response to the air around it, scanning the air 3,600 times per hour. The filter lasts up to a whopping six years, and it can clean up to 1,650 square feet in an hour. This model has an updated LCD screen that has tons of information about the air around you, including metrics with graphics about air insights; historical graphs on air quality, temperature, and humidity; and pollutant information, including measurements for PM 2.5 and 10, and VOCs. To be honest, though, this air purifier slightly annoyed me. The bottom never seemed to screw in right and often fell out, and the fan auto-detected seemingly any and every potential pollutant on auto mode—something as innocuous as my cat walking by would launch it into its highest level, at about 75 decibels. When I conducted a test with smoke pellets in a sealed tent, the purifier didn’t auto-adjust to the pollutants; I had to manually enter and hit the button to engage it. Then the air quality was at zero percent on the screen for 15 minutes, the smoke didn’t visually clear, and it seemed as if it wasn’t actually purifying. When I went to check on what was happening, I accidentally restarted the purifier and it took almost five hours for the monitor to read that it was at a healthy level again.

Coway Airmega Halo for $230: This is the newest release in Coway's Airmega line: an affordable, lightweight air purifier that aims to deliver whole-room air purification at an accessible price point. It's a lightweight 9.7 pounds and doesn't have Wi-Fi capabilities, an app, or a remote. Inside, there's a cylindrical IEST-certified HEPA three-stage filter and a MegaScan Particle Sensor, which continuously monitors the air in real time to detect smoke, fine dust, and allergens down to PM2.5. As I do with all WIRED-tested air purifiers, I measured the Airmega Halo's efficacy by using a sealed tent and smoke pellets to see how quickly each air purifier clears the pellet smoke and returns the air to healthy quality when on auto mode. After one minute and 45 seconds, the air was no longer clouded and the light shone blue for a healthy level. However, in independent testing with an air quality monitor, I found that it took nearly six minutes for the air to truly return to normal levels again—an alarming, almost-four-minute discrepancy. Still, if you're looking for a purifier for a baby's room or are an especially light sleeper, this purifier offers a Night Sensor feature that could be helpful.

IQAir CG MultiGas XE Photograph: Lisa Wood Shapiro

IQAir GC MultiGas XE for $1,600: This Swiss-made unit is a heavy tower model (55 pounds), but it has wheels for easier rolling, and at its highest setting, it can clean 275 cubic feet per minute (CFM). I appreciate that the air sensor’s indicator light is in accordance with US AQI colors. And the built-in sensor and IQAir app make it easy to use—in fact, the app provides one of the most intuitive user experiences of all I’ve tested. It can also capture toxic gases and vapors, and on auto mode, the fan speeds auto-adjust. It can clean the air of a large space with multiple air exchanges in an hour. I’ve been using it in the main room of an A-frame cabin with double-height ceilings (around 3,000 cubic feet) for the past two months, and it has kept my indoor air quality healthy. But with great power comes great noise. At its highest setting, the CG MultiGas XE runs at a loud 68 decibels—that's just 2 decibels shy of the sound of a consumer vacuum cleaner, though it’s quiet at its lower settings. At $1,600, this workhorse isn’t cheap, but it’s an investment that’s built to last. —Lisa Wood Shapiro

Airthings Renew Photograph: Lisa Wood Shapiro

Airthings Renew for $300: I wasn’t expecting to like the unassuming minimalist Renew from Airthings as much as I did. Its gray box design is so understated, quiet, and powerful that it was easy to plug it in and forget about it. The Renew is also the first purifier I’ve tested that gives the user multiple placement options: It can stand up with the air output facing up and sideways, and the entire box can lie on the floor. The Airthings app not only shows data graph-style, but it also functions as a remote that can adjust the purifier settings, including setting the panel lock, which is handy for cat owners. The control panel and the indicator light are barely there, and it’s not easy to see the tiny light letting me know my indoor air quality. At first, I thought the main drawback was size. The Renew is made for a bedroom, home office, or nursery. If you place it in a larger room, it’s going to have to run at its highest setting. The main drawback that I noticed after several months of use was the exterior prefilter. It did its job capturing pollutants, but I wasn't able to clean it, even with my vacuum. —Lisa Wood Shapiro

Coway Airmega ProX for $905: The Coway Airmega ProX is a monolith any high-ceilinged home needs. Specifically, if you’re living in an A-frame, double-height ceiling loft, or any home with a ceiling higher than 8 feet, this model is for you. It gives off the vibe of a TARS robot from Interstellar crossed with a giant stereo speaker. It has a nice blend-into-the-room-mocha beige aesthetic and can clean the air four times per hour in a 1,000-square-foot space when running at its highest setting. And even at its highest and therefore loudest setting, it hovers around 50 decibels, slightly louder than the sound of falling rain, making it one of the quieter large tower air purifiers I’ve tested. It also has a control panel lock that is a plus for parents and cat owners alike. However, even though the 50-pound ProX has hidden handles and built-in lockable wheels, it really is just too heavy for the home consumer. —Lisa Wood Shapiro

Coway Airmega 400S Photograph: Lisa Wood Shapiro

Coway Airmega 400S for $646: Coway's Airmega 400S is another banger from the air purifier innovators. The 400S checks all the boxes when it comes to features. It has a reliable auto mode that adjusts the fan speed according to the air quality using its built-in air quality sensor. It also has a timer to schedule one, four, or eight hours of running time. And while it has a serviceable app, its built-in air sensor and auto-adjust fan keep me from having to micromanage settings. The question is, can this air purifier do the job without me pushing buttons or checking the indoor air quality, and do it quietly? With the Airmega 400S, the answer is yes. I just wish its 15 x 23 x 15-inch dimensions didn't make it so hard to place in a room. —Lisa Wood Shapiro

AirDoctor AD4000 Air Purifier for $429: AirDoctor makes sturdy and reliable purifiers, but as I went to pair the AD4000, I realized it had no Wi-Fi button on the control panel. At 15 pounds and nearly $800, the AD4000 should be Wi-Fi compatible, especially since it has an internal air quality sensor. Users should have the option to view indoor air quality on the AirDoctor app dashboard. And while the AD4000 is made for larger spaces, if one wanted to achieve the four air exchanges per hour that the AD4000 supposedly can do, then it would have its fan at the highest setting. My consumer sound level meter registered 100 decibels at full blast. It sounded to me like a hair dryer on a low setting. For context, the CDC’s recommendation for noise levels for workers is that they are not exposed to 100 decibels for more than 15 minutes. It’s for that reason that all air purifiers need to be in a space where they can run the fan at the lowest (or reasonably quiet) setting. The AD4000 would do well in a 200- to 300-square-foot room, where it could run on a lower setting. Also, be careful when unboxing: When I was setting up the AD4000, the sticker with instructions to take the filters out of their plastic bags pulled off the control panel when I went to remove it. —Lisa Wood Shapiro

Airdog X5 for $549: The Airdog X5 is the first washable-filter air purifier I’ve tested. And while it doesn’t use a HEPA, it is California Air Resources Board–certified. CARB lists it as electronic filtration instead of a HEPA filter; that would be listed as mechanical. As I’ve written before, if an air purifier isn’t CARB-certified, it's likely not worth buying. I tested the Airdog in a large room, and it even came with a limited-edition pet plate. That is exactly what it sounds like—a plate that fits over the Airdog meant for a cat to perch on. Neither of my cats took to it. The Airdog has a responsive built-in sensor that was in sync with my other air quality monitors. And its electronic air filters, by way of their patented TPA technology, charge particles and then capture them. The best way I can describe it is to imagine that the PM 2.5 are mosquitoes and the Airdog is like an old-time mosquito zapper. It works a little like that, and if the filter gets dirty enough, it will make zap sounds. —Lisa Wood Shapiro

Windmill Air Purifier for $299: I like the Scandinavian look of this bamboo purifier, and it’s more furniture-esque than other models. Still, with the blue model, the nicks in the veneer show up as white. It’s possible the bamboo finish might wear better. I really like this brand and reviewed its desk fan and air conditioner, the latter of which pairs with the Windmill Air app, and I'm equally happy using the app with its air purifier. The Windmill has an internal sensor and indicator light: green for good, yellow for moderate, pink for bad, and red for unhealthy. And while the “boost” setting is the loudest, it is still relatively quiet at its lower setting. I prefer to run it on the auto-adjusting eco mode. —Lisa Wood Shapiro

Coway Airmega 50 for $80: A mini version of the brand's Airmega 100, the Airmega 50 (see the full review) has many of the features of Coway’s larger and more expensive models and is notably affordable. The Airmega 50 was surprisingly effective for an air purifier the size of a roll of paper towels. The built-in sensor triggers both auto mode and the air quality indicator light, which gives the user instant information with nightlight vibes. One issue I have with all Coway air purifiers is the fact the custom color air quality indicator lights are different from the US AQI's six color-coded categories. Instead of green signaling good air, Coway’s green means air quality is moderate. See how it’s confusing? Blue, which is not on the US AQI color scale, means good.

Photograph: Lisa Wood Shapiro

Puroair 240 HEPA Air Purifier for $160: At less than 9 inches tall, the Puroair 240 is tiny. And like so many of the smaller tabletop models, it’s also loud. It might be effective in a small space, say a room about 100 to 150 square feet. It's also CARB-certified. I found its filter size too small to effectively clean an average-sized room. And while I still review smaller air purifiers, there are larger and quieter models on the market for relatively the same cost that have greater air exchanges in a larger-sized room. The Puroair’s indicator light is adjusted by the 240’s internal sensor and is green for acceptable, yellow for moderate, and red for poor air quality. At times, I found the thin sliver of the indicator’s light difficult to see. The 240 has auto or manual mode, a timer, child lock, and filter replacement light. It also has a three-stage filter, including the tightly woven HEPA 14, activated carbon, and prefilter. Lastly, the 240’s black plastic attracted a noticeable amount of fingerprints. —Lisa Wood Shapiro

Coway Airmega 250 for $380: The Airmega 250 has a decently large footprint, but it’s rated to clean a 930-square-foot room twice an hour. That’s why I put it smack-dab in the middle of the first floor of my home to clean the air in my kitchen and living room. Every time I cook, the smart air purifier mode automatically detects unhealthy particles in the air and ratchets up the fan’s power. It also recently did this when I had someone patch some drywall in my mudroom. (This mode works with the help of a PM10 and PM2.5 particle sensor.) The fan at its highest setting isn’t that loud—I measured it at 60 decibels standing right in front of it. There’s a sleep mode if you want it silent. You get the usual controls, like timer functionality and replacement indicators for the filter. Speaking of, the Airmega 250 uses a true HEPA filter that needs to be replaced once every six to 12 months. This, combined with the washable prefilter that you should be keeping clean every two weeks and the activated carbon filter, allows the air purifier to remove 99.999 percent of ultrafine particles down to 0.01 microns, or so Coway says. It’s super easy to remove these filters to clean and swap them out. The whole system is roughly 21 pounds, so you can move it around fairly easily. Coway offers a three-year warranty. The Coway Airmega 250S is the same model but with Wi-Fi functionality, so you can control it via an app and see more details. The last thing I need is another app, but maybe you don’t mind. —Julian Chokkattu

Oransi AirMend Photograph: Lisa Wood Shapiro

Oransi AirMend True Carbon for $350: While other AirMend models are made for HEPA filters, the True Carbon doesn’t have a HEPA. Instead, it has a 3-pound activated carbon filter. There's a remote but no internal sensor, so raising the fan speed is a manual operation. It took a few tries using the remote, as there is a small lag time as the fan adjusts to different speeds. I appreciated the magnetic remote holder on the top of the purifier. It’s quiet on most settings and has an easy-to-miss minimalist design, blending into most spaces. The True Carbon is for those who need serious odor removal. I placed the True Carbon next to my two cats’ heavily used litter box, and within half hour the purifier eliminated the smell. I knew it was working when my son couldn’t detect an odor. I could see the True Carbon being an essential appliance for smoker households, kitchens that retain smells, or cat owners. It’s surprisingly effective, but this is for VOCs and odors. The True Carbon is HEPA-less—it cannot capture fine particulates from the air. What you gain with a supersized activated carbon filter, you lose in standard air purifying ability such as removing PM2.5. That might be fine for your needs. Oransi also makes a wall mount and handy travel bag sold separately. —Lisa Wood Shapiro

PurOxygen P500i for $170: This machine cleans the air of a smaller-than-average-sized room, and its easy-to-read display, app compatibility, side handles, and unique all-in-one filter make it easy to like. I usually stay away from small-room air purifiers due to their loud noise and less-than-ideal air-cleaning power. And while at its highest setting, the P500i reaches up to 50 decibels, it operates quietly at lower speeds and can effectively clean the air in a home office or a room smaller than 200 square feet. The PurOxygen uses a combined filter that has a prefilter that can be un-Velcroed and hand-washed, an activated carbon, a HEPA 13, and a cold catalyst filter. A cold catalyst, also known as low-temperature catalyst filtration, can cause a chemical reaction that can break down gases, like VOCs, and convert them to less harmful substances. And while the P5001 is CARB-certified as a mechanical air purifier, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) does not recommend catalysts due to their limited effectiveness. —Lisa Wood Shapiro

Still, for sheer sonic superiority, the Focal Mu-So Hekla is one of my all-time favorite soundbars.

Honorable Mentions

Sonos Beam Gen 2 for $499: The Sonos Beam Gen 2 is an excellent compact soundbar options, especially if you have other Sonos speakers in your home.
